title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Worn Surface Evolution Using Convolutional LSTM With Adaptive Filtering and Recursive Multi-Step Prediction
affiliations: Yonsei University, Yonsei University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Worn Surface Evolution Using Convolutional LSTM With Adaptive Filtering and Recursive Multi-Step Prediction
detail.abstract: Reliable prediction of the spatiotemporal evolution ofwear-induced surface topography is critical for assessing the reliability of sliding-contact mechanical components, yet most data-driven studies remain focused on scalar wear indicators. This study presents a Convolutional LSTM(Long Short-Term Memory)-based model that directly forecasts future height maps from limited earlystage time-series observations. The AI contribution is a distribution-aware, KDE (kernel density estimation)-based adaptive filtering rule embedded in recursive multi-step forecasting: the threshold is updated from the incremental-wear density (valley between near-zero noise and wear components) to suppress unworn-region false positives and prevent error accumulation. The engineering application is long-horizon, field-level prediction of worn-surface evolution to complement contact–wear simulations and reduce reliance on full-duration wear testing in reliability assessment and surfacedesign screening. Across recursive prediction up to 10,000 cycles, the proposed framework preserves wear-scar topology and surface statistical trends, achieving SSIM of 0.9904 at 10,000 cycles and tracking cumulative wear volume with an average relative error of 3.94% over 3,500 – 10,000 cycles.

title: Targeted and non-targeted per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) characterization in irrigation waters across Albania
affiliations: Agriculture University of Tirana, University of Massachusetts Lowell, University of Massachusetts Lowell, Agriculture University of Tirana, Albanian Academy of Sciences, Albanian University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Tirana and University of Massachusetts Lowell

detail.title: Targeted and non-targeted per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) characterization in irrigation waters across Albania
detail.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are an emerging environmental concern in agriculture due to their persistence, mobility, and potential to enter the food chain through irrigation. This study presents the first nationwide assessment of PFAS occurrence in surface and groundwater used for irrigation across Albania. Seventy-seven water samples were collected from (i) surface water irrigation sites (rivers, streams, and reservoirs), (ii) groundwater systems (wells), and (iii) water bodies located near industrial sites with potential PFAS discharges. Samples were analyzed using complementary targeted and non-targeted mass spectrometry approaches: 1) targeted quantification of 46 PFAS by LC–ESI–MS/MS and 2) high-resolution non-targeted screening against a PFAS database of ~7,000 structures using LC–HR–QTOF–MS/MS. Targeted analysis detected 22 PFAS, dominated by ultra and short-chain compounds (C2–C6). Perfluoropropionic acid (PFPrA, C3) was present in 100% of samples, whereas long-chain legacy PFAS (C7–C12), including PFOS and PFOA, were detected less frequently (3–23%). The sum of detectable PFAS (ΣPFAS) concentrations ranged from 4.7 to 2.2 × 10⁶ ng/L, with the highest levels detected in waters influenced by hospital and oil-processing effluents. Non-targeted screening of seven samples identified 13 additional PFAS, including perfluoroalkane sulfonamido amines (PFSAAm) and fluorotelomer sulfonates (FTS). Elevated concentrations near industrial and hospital discharges underscore the need for regulatory monitoring and improved effluent treatment. By integrating targeted and non-targeted analytical approaches, this study provides a more comprehensive characterization of PFAS diversity in irrigation waters and establishes a baseline for future national monitoring and agricultural risk assessment in Albania.

title: Deep Learning for Distributed Acoustic Sensing–Based Microseismic Event Detection in Enhanced Geothermal Systems: A Comparative Study of Twelve Architectures
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Universiti Teknologi Petronas and Universitas Islam Indonesia

detail.title: Deep Learning for Distributed Acoustic Sensing–Based Microseismic Event Detection in Enhanced Geothermal Systems: A Comparative Study of Twelve Architectures
detail.abstract: Microseismic event detection in distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) data is critical for monitoring enhanced geothermal system (EGS) operations, yet classical detectors based on short-term to long-term energy ratios fail to discriminate genuine seismic arrivals from structured noise. This paper presents a comparative study of twelve deep learning architectures spanning five families—convolutional neural networks, transformers, recurrent networks, state-space models, and graph neural networks—benchmarked against three classical baselines on 3,974 manually labeled DAS recordings from a field stimulation campaign. We contribute an open-source labeling tool for multichannel seismic data, and demonstrate that full-recording classification (1200 ms) yields a +14 pp F1 improvement over short-window approaches. The best-performing convolutional model achieves 98.50% F1 and 99.46% AUC with a 26-fold false-alarm reduction over the classical baseline. A selective state-space model achieves 95.76% F1, establishing a competitive baseline for this architecture family. A graph neural network exploiting fiber spatial topology achieves 95.47% F1 with only 94,290 parameters. Gradient-weighted class activation mapping confirms that the convolutional models learn physically meaningful P-wave moveout patterns. Zero-shot cross-stage evaluation shows that the learned representations generalize across stimulation stages without retraining, while the classical detector degrades by 13.6 pp.

title: Linking socio-economic dynamics across regional scales to assess land-atmosphere feedbacks of land cover change
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Bonn, Columbia University, University of Minnesota - St. Paul - Institute on the Environment, University of Bonn and University of Bonn

detail.title: Linking socio-economic dynamics across regional scales to assess land-atmosphere feedbacks of land cover change
detail.abstract: Anthropogenic land cover change is a potentially important driver of regional climate dynamics, yet its integration into climate assessments remains limited. This study showcases a new approach that allows socio-economic development assumptions to propagate from global economic dynamics to local land-atmosphere feedbacks. The framework loosely couples (1) land cover projections consistent with the five Shared Socio-Economic Pathways from a global economic model, (2) a high-resolution land cover downscaling model, and (3) a high-resolution regional climate model coupling land-atmosphere interactions. Moderate land cover changes (2.7% - 7.9% of the study area) produce measurable biophysical feedbacks leading to three key findings. First, deforestation and urbanization emerge as dominant drivers of regional temperature increases. Second, land-atmosphere feedbacks to land cover change are strongest during the crop growing season (April - October). Third, these feedbacks are particularly relevant in low-emission mitigation scenarios involving substantial land cover interventions. Overall, this study’s results demonstrate that socio-economic drivers of land cover change, even if moderate, can significantly influence regional climate patterns. Integrating land-atmosphere feedbacks into climate assessments through coupled socio-economic and biophysical modeling is therefore essential for robust regional climate projections and for informed adaptation and mitigation planning.

title: Economic Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants Based on Improved Fixed-Time Consistency Algorithm
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Zhejiang University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Economic Scheduling of Virtual Power Plants Based on Improved Fixed-Time Consistency Algorithm

keywords.keywords: equal incremental cost；optimization and control；virtual power plants；power balance

detail.abstract: This paper addresses the dynamic changes in virtual power plant (VPP) communication topologies and plug-and-play requirements of distributed units by proposing an improved fixed-time distributed consensus algorithm, which is applied to solve the VPP optimization and control problem. The incremental costs of distributed generation units, energy storage incremental costs, and controllable load incremental benefits are designated as consensus variables. A distributed consensus-based optimization and control framework is established, relying solely on local information and neighbor-to-neighbor communication. To enhance convergence performance, a gradient gain coefficient and power deviation compensation mechanism are introduced into the traditional consensus algorithm's global cost function gradient term, thereby forming an improved consensus algorithm with fixed-time convergence characteristics. Based on Lyapunov stability theory and algebraic graph theory, rigorous derivations of convergence criteria and stability boundary conditions for the proposed algorithm are provided. Case studies and analyses validate the effectiveness and robustness of the optimization and control strategy, demonstrating its capability to accommodate VPP topological variations and plug-and-play functionalities.

title: Designing training plans for a multiskilled workforce under demand uncertainty: Integrating employer objectives and employee preferences
affiliations: Universidad del Norte, Universidad de los Andes and Universidad Andrés Bello

detail.title: Designing training plans for a multiskilled workforce under demand uncertainty: Integrating employer objectives and employee preferences
detail.abstract: Multiskilling is a workforce flexibility strategy that enables employees to perform multiple tasks effectively. This paper addresses a personnel training problem by incorporating multiskilling through a k-chaining policy with k≥2, while explicitly considering three key employee training preferences. A two-stage stochastic optimization model is proposed to minimize total training costs and the expected costs associated with overstaffing and understaffing, while incorporating penalties and rewards linked to employee preferences. In this way, the model simultaneously seeks to reduce employer costs and enhance employee satisfaction. The proposed methodology is evaluated through a real-world retail case study using processed and simulated data from a Chilean store. Four experiments and nine levels of demand variability are analyzed. The results show that incorporating employee preferences, either partially or fully, does not significantly affect employer costs or overall multiskilling requirements, while substantially improving employee satisfaction. This suggests that employer and employee objectives are not necessarily conflicting, enabling the design of training plans that benefit both parties. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses on key preference parameters indicate that, although these parameters influence workforce composition, their impact on costs and multiskilling levels remains limited, confirming the stability of the proposed solution.

title: Does Social Support Matter More than Education in Shaping Women’s Entrepreneurial Intentions?
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Does Social Support Matter More than Education in Shaping Women’s Entrepreneurial Intentions?
detail.abstract: A B S T R A C TEntrepreneurship education (EE) is often promoted to foster entrepreneurial intention (EI), yet evidence remains mixed, particularly for women facing structural barriers. This study explores whether social support (SS) matters more than EE in shaping women’s entrepreneurial intentions, considering the roles of entrepreneurial self-efficacy (ESE), digital skills (DS), and perceived gender barriers (PGB). Survey data from 358 undergraduates were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and fuzzy set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA). The results show that EE enhances ESE and DS but has no direct effect on EI; rather, ESE is the strongest predictor, mediating EE’s influence, while DS plays a weaker supporting role. SS strengthens the effect of ESE on EI, whereas PGB reduces the impact of DS. FsQCA confirmed multiple sufficient pathways, with ESE consistently central and reduced PGB enabling intention. Importance-Performance Matrix Analysis (IPMA) further identified ESE and SS as the most influential drivers. The findings highlight that confidence and social support, more than education alone, drive women’s entrepreneurial motivation.

title: WHERE: Weekly Hypergraph Evolving Representation Learning for Next POI Recommendation
affiliations: Shanghai Normal University, Shanghai Normal University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shanghai Normal University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: WHERE: Weekly Hypergraph Evolving Representation Learning for Next POI Recommendation
detail.abstract: Next Point-of-Interest (POI) recommendation is a pivotal task in location-based services (LBS), aiming to predict users' future movement based on their historical trajectories. However, existing methods often model check-ins using static sequences or static graphs, failing to capture both high-order structural dependencies among POIs and their long-term temporal evolution. To address these limitations, we propose Weekly Hypergraph Evolving Representation Learning (WHERE) for next POI recommendation, which unifies local high-order dependencies and global temporal evolution to learn dynamic POI representations. Specifically, WHERE first constructs multi-view weekly hypergraphs to integrate collaborative, geographical, and categorical signals within fine-grained time windows. To effectively aggregate these heterogeneous structures, we design a dual-attention hypergraph convolution module that adaptively weights informative nodes and hyperedges, followed by an adaptive gating mechanism for multi-view fusion. Crucially, we introduce a global temporal evolution module featuring a GRU-based activity-contingent sparse update strategy. This mechanism dynamically maintains global memory by selectively evolving POIs that appear in the current week, while strictly preserving the latent states of all others. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that WHERE consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in terms of recommendation accuracy. Source codes are available at https://github.com/liuzilin123/WHERE.

title: Nonlinear marginal returns in higher-order public goods games
affiliations: Hangzhou Normal University, Hangzhou Normal University, Hangzhou Normal University and Hangzhou Normal University

detail.title: Nonlinear marginal returns in higher-order public goods games
detail.abstract: Understanding how cooperation persists under higher-order interactions and nonlinear payoff accumulation remains a central problem in evolutionary dynamics and complex systems. Here, we investigate an evolutionary public goods game on random hypergraphs with a threshold-controlled marginal return mechanism. Cooperative contributions generate synergistic amplification below a critical threshold, whereas excessive participation induces strict discounting due to saturation effects. By combining microscopic Fermi updating with macroscopic replicator dynamics, we analytically derive the transcritical and saddle-node bifurcation boundaries governing the global phase structure. The system exhibits four dynamical regimes: defection dominance, bistability, coexistence, and full cooperation. Notably, our analysis proves that the inevitable crowding effect mathematically precludes direct bi-stability between pure defection and pure cooperation. We further identify a "structural squeeze" effect at low thresholds, where premature saturation severely restricts the stability of pure cooperation. Increasing the critical synergy threshold effectively mitigates this crowding penalty and fundamentally alters the transition topology, inducing a shift from continuous (second-order) phase transitions to discontinuous (first-order) macroscopic jumps. Furthermore, we demonstrate that proportionally scaling the synergy threshold with group size substantially lowers the saddle-node boundary and exponentially enlarges the bistable region. These results reveal how higher-order interactions and threshold-dependent nonlinear returns jointly reshape collective evolutionary trajectories.

title: Towards the evolution of Earth Observation in Europe: A methodology for comparing institutional space governance models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Towards the evolution of Earth Observation in Europe: A methodology for comparing institutional space governance models
detail.abstract: Historically, States and a few large private-sector entities have dominated national space activities, investing in the Earth observation (EO) sector to achieve technological and scientific objectives and address political, security, and industrial interests. Now, rapid technological advancements, shifts in the geopolitical security landscape, the growing importance of situational awareness, and increased global competition are transforming governance structures in the space sector. In this evolving context, institutional governance must integrate emerging private actors, balancing competitiveness and innovation with the need to address potential threats to safety, security, and sustainability. To examine the evolution and maturity of Earth Observation governance in Europe, we conducted a comparative governance analysis and reviewed the state of the art globally. Our research focuses on nine selected countries and the multi-level governance case of the European Union, a supranational union of States. Then, we developed a comparative assessment based on key interdisciplinary parameters. These parameters include the maturity of national space law, the implementation status of public-private partnerships (PPPs), and governance and technological capacity, such as national EO missions, ground stations, and spaceports. The findings contribute to governance knowledge by providing a scalable model for evaluating state governance performance and by presenting a qualitative and semi-quantitative analytical framework for understanding the evolution of EO governance patterns.

title: Regulation, Intermediaries, and the Emergence of Dual-Loop Circularity in Durable Goods Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Regulation, Intermediaries, and the Emergence of Dual-Loop Circularity in Durable Goods Markets
detail.abstract: This paper studies how regulation and intermediaries jointly shape circularity in secondary markets for durable goods. Motivated by the European used vehicle market, where strict inspection regimes coexist with large intermediaries, we develop a model in which a material loop of product flows is coupled with a customer loop of transactions. The intermediary absorbs products that would otherwise be scrapped and reallocates them across markets, including export destinations with lower regulatory thresholds, thereby linking heterogeneous regulatory environments.We show that the relationship between regulatory stringency and scrappage is non-monotonic. Stricter regulation can initially reduce scrappage by expanding the intermediary’s absorption region, but beyond a threshold it increases disposal when capacity constraints depress intermediary prices. We further demonstrate that customer retention, typically viewed as beneficial, has a regime-dependent effect: while stronger retention increases transaction internalization under slack capacity, it can generate congestion that reduces intermediary absorption and raises scrappage.The analysis yields three main insights. First, circularity in secondary markets emerges endogenously from the interaction between regulation and intermediary capacity, rather than from centrally designed recovery systems. Second, intermediary pricing and capacity jointly determine allocation outcomes across repair, resale, export, and disposal, linking operational constraints with lifecycle decisions. Third, the viability of the system is governed by a dual-loop feasibility condition, requiring a balance between material inflow and customer retention; outside this region, the system cannot sustain circular flows.These findings provide a new perspective on circular economy systems by highlighting intermediaries as stabilizing agents between regulatory pressure and market demand, and by identifying the conditions under which circularity can be sustained or disrupted. The results have implications for both firm strategy and policy design in regulated durable goods markets.

title: Estimating Historical Fluctuations of the European Space Agency's Budget
affiliations: International Space University

detail.title: Estimating Historical Fluctuations of the European Space Agency's Budget
detail.abstract: The European Space Agency (ESA) has been a multilateral financial initiative, with monetary contributions from its member states, since the inception of its predecessors, ELDO and ESRO, in the 1960s. Its financial resources have evolved since then; however, there has been no comprehensive analysis or data collection of its budgetary progression, especially before the creation of the Euro in 1999. This research study examines historical financial archives from 1961 to 2025, both on a nominal basis and on a real basis, adjusting the financial data for currency and inflation fluctuations. To address the currency value conundrum, this study develops a U.S. Dollar exchange rate index for the Euro's predecessor, the European Currency Unit (ECU). This research finds that ESA has spent over €360 billion over its 65-year existence, and its annual budget has experienced multiple historical peaks of around $7.2 to $8.8 billion, followed by drops of 52-61% to $3.4 billion, adjusted to 2025 inflation. This study concludes with a historical trend comparison of ISRO and NASA budgets, and a static intra-European comparison of 2024/25 space budget contributions, especially on a per-capita basis (roughly €15.2), and member state contributions to ESA activities and programmes (an average of 71.02% for 2013-25). Research approaches from this study, including the ECU index and the data-collection methodology for ESA historical archives, could be applied in future research to investigate and address potential ESA financial issues.

title: Social Mobility in the Russia of Revolutions, 1879-2016: A Surname Study
affiliations: , University of Southern Denmark, National Research University Higher School of Economics (Moscow) and National Research University Higher School of Economics (Moscow)

detail.title: Social Mobility in the Russia of Revolutions, 1879-2016: A Surname Study
detail.abstract: Russian surname types differed substantially in average social status prior to the Revolution of 1917. Using this, and tracking these surname types to the present, we show that despite enormous social turmoil in Russia, the underlying rate of social mobility increased little compared to the Czarist era, and compared to such institutionally stable societies as England. The measure we have of elite social status is educational attainment measured by attendance at Moscow State University. The noble surname types of 1879 are still overrepresented among the students of Moscow State University in 2016. Despite the initial drop in implied intergenerational persistence of educational status around the Revolution, overall persistence of the entire century is still around 0.7, only marginally less than the 0.8 observed in England or in Czarist Russia.

title: The Death of King Coal and the Scars of Deindustrialization
affiliations: NHH Norwegian School of Economics and University of Nottingham

detail.title: The Death of King Coal and the Scars of Deindustrialization
detail.abstract: The post-war collapse of the British coal industry was one of the most dramatic episodes of de-industrialisation in post-war Britain and one of the largest energy transitions of thetwentieth century, yet its human costs remain poorly documented. Using longitudinaldata following two cohorts born in 1958 and 1970, we provide the first systematic evidence on its lifelong consequences. Children exposed to the shock have had worse healththroughout life, and this effect has transmitted over generations. They were also raised inless privileged economic conditions and accumulated less wealth as adults. Our findingsdocument that in the absence of targeted support, the transition away from coal imposedlong-lasting human costs on the communities left behind. Few people moved, and thosewho did still kept a scar.

title: Credit-Market Segmentation, Monetary Transmission, and Fiscal-Financial Stress in a Small Open Economy
affiliations: Universidad Pablo de Olavide, Universidade Federal da Paraíba and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Credit-Market Segmentation, Monetary Transmission, and Fiscal-Financial Stress in a Small Open Economy
detail.abstract: This paper studies how credit-market segmentation affects monetary transmission and stabilization trade-offs in a small open economy facing fiscal-financial stress. In many emerging economies, a significant share of private borrowing is supplied through directed, regulated, earmarked, subsidized, or publicly supported credit lines that are only partially exposed to the policy rate. We embed this protected-credit segment into a tradable--nontradable small open economy with sticky nontradable prices, working-capital finance,sovereign-financial spreads, and inflation-targeting monetary policy.The model compares a market-credit benchmark, an economy with a structural protected-credit segment, and an economy in which protected credit expands endogenously under stress. Credit-market segmentation weakens aggregate monetary pass-through because part of borrowing is insulated from policy-rate increases. As a result, the central bank raises the policy rate more aggressively, but the effective borrowing rate responds less than in the market-credit benchmark. Protected credit therefore cushions real activity and privateconsumption, while making nominal stabilization less effective.The cost is fiscal-financial. Under the Brazil-disciplined benchmark calibration, economies with protected credit experience smaller realcontractions but higher inflation, stronger nominal depreciation, wider sovereign-financial spreads, positive parafiscal subsidy costs, and greater public-debt stress. The main quantitative discontinuity is between the market-credit economy and economies with a structural protected-credit segment; stress-contingent protected-credit expansion provides additional but moderate amplification. Credit-market segmentation is therefore not a clean aggregate stabilizer: it protects selected borrowers, but shifts the stabilization burden toward inflation, the exchange rate, sovereign spreads, and the fiscal-parafiscal block.

title: Self-Leadership as a Microfoundation of Leadership: Integrating Intrapersonal Self-Influence With Relational and Collective Leadership Theories
affiliations: Grand Canyon University

detail.title: Self-Leadership as a Microfoundation of Leadership: Integrating Intrapersonal Self-Influence With Relational and Collective Leadership Theories
detail.abstract: Leadership research has predominantly conceptualized leadership as interpersonal influence, emphasizing leader behaviors, leader-follower relationships, and collective processes. Yet contemporary work increasingly requires individuals to regulate their own motivation, attention, emotion, and persistence in contexts where leader influence is intermittent, indirect, or distributed. Self-leadership - the repertoire of learned self-influence strategies through which individuals direct their own behavior and cognition - offers a theoretically grounded account of this intrapersonal influence system. Despite a substantial literature, self-leadership remains inconsistently integrated into mainstream leadership theories and is often treated as adjacent to empowerment rather than as a foundational explanatory mechanism. This article positions self-leadership as a microfoundation of leadership and advances an integrative multilevel framework specifying three roles it plays in leadership systems. First, self-leadership functions as a mechanism translating leader behaviors into sustained execution. Second, it operates as a boundary condition shaping when interpersonal leadership is substitutable, complementary, or necessary. Third, it acts as a catalyst enabling the emergence and effectiveness of shared leadership. We clarify construct boundaries, identify proximal mechanisms and boundary conditions, and develop testable propositions. The article concludes with a research agenda emphasizing falsifiability, multilevel designs, temporal ordering, and identification strategies consistent with rigorous leadership science.

title: Corporate Worker Health Orientation and Innovation Under Risk Cross-National Evidence
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Bologna, Department of Statistical Sciences and University of Bologna- Department of Management

detail.title: Corporate Worker Health Orientation and Innovation Under Risk Cross-National Evidence
detail.abstract: Despite extensive research showing that firms reduce long-term innovation investment under risk, less attention has been devoted to why some firms sustain or even increase innovation while others retreat. This study examines whether corporate workers’ health orientation functions as a firm-level capability that enables firms to sustain innovation under risk. Using a cross-national panel dataset of 36,691 firm-year observations from 5,358 publicly listed firms across 32 countries (2005–2024), we analyze the relationships among innovation, risk, and worker-oriented practices using fixed-effects regressions and subsample analyses. Results show that corporate worker health orientation is positively associated with innovation, while risk is negatively associated with innovation. Importantly, corporate worker health orientation moderates this relationship: as risk increases, firms with stronger worker-oriented systems experience a weaker decline in innovation, and at sufficiently high levels, the relationship becomes positive. These findings position worker-oriented systems as a key microfoundation of organizational resilience, explaining heterogeneity in firms’ strategic responses to risk.

title: A Multi-Scale Urban Metabolism Assessment Using Environmental-Economic Accounting: Evidence from Metropolitan Guatemala
affiliations: Universidad Rafael Landívar and

detail.title: A Multi-Scale Urban Metabolism Assessment Using Environmental-Economic Accounting: Evidence from Metropolitan Guatemala
detail.abstract: This study develops and applies a downscaling protocol that translates national System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA) accounts to the municipal scale, addressing a methodological gap that has limited urban metabolism research in data-scarce metropolitan contexts. The framework is applied to Guatemala’s metropolitan region, comprising 28 municipalities and 3.5 million inhabitants across three nested spatial scales, by integrating SEEA departmental accounts for 2019 with census data, infrastructure inventories, and geospatial imagery. The results reveal a predominantly linear metabolism in which 93% of water supply derives from unregulated private wells, only 3% of wastewater receives municipal treatment, and firewood supplies 54% of regional energy alongside 35% from fossil fuels. The sectoral structure varies sharply across scales, with commerce and services consuming 63% of water in the core, and agriculture 44% in the polycentric periphery, while residential firewood combustion accounts for 77% of household greenhouse gas emissions. Under current trends, approximately 500,000 residents will inhabit flood- and landslide-prone areas by 2032. The SEEA framework captures hidden flows that utility-based assessments systematically miss, and the methodology is directly replicable in any country with national SEEA accounts.

title: Gender and Institutional Trust in Latin America and the Caribbean
affiliations: Pontificia Universidad Javeriana

detail.title: Gender and Institutional Trust in Latin America and the Caribbean
detail.abstract: This paper documents a region-specific gender gap in institutional trust. Using the World Values Survey, I show that women in Latin America and the Caribbean report lower institutional trust than men, and that this gap is more negative than in most other regions. The gap is concentrated in state and political institutions, especially institutions of authority and representation. A smaller within-region gap also appears for interpersonal trust, but the regional differential is concentrated in institutional trust. The result is robust to specification, weighting, and composition checks. Latinobarómetro provides complementary evidence, especially for trust in the armed forces.

title: Workplace Control Without Anger: A Qualitative Within-Organization Study of Mistake Correction, Psychological Safety, and Organizational Learning
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Workplace Control Without Anger: A Qualitative Within-Organization Study of Mistake Correction, Psychological Safety, and Organizational Learning
detail.abstract:
This paper presents an exploratory qualitative within-organization study of how workplace control can be maintained without relying on anger. Based on approximately three years of observational experience in one workplace and approximately seven months of continuous observation in another workplace within the same Japanese organization, the study compares anger-based and non-anger-based responses to mistakes, responsibility confirmation, and error correction.
 The study compares two workplace environments within the same organization. In one workplace, anger, public reprimands, negative labeling, emotional intimidation, and silencing were observed as part of workplace control. There, mistakes and deficiencies were likely to be transformed from mere objects of correction into materials for evaluating an individual's ability, attitude, hierarchy, and value as a member of the workplace. In contrast, in the other workplace, although work-related warnings, responsibility confirmation, recurrence prevention, and error correction were indeed carried out, they were implemented without raised voices or personal denigration, through calm confirmation, explanation of reasons, gentle correction requests, and relationship maintenance accompanied by laughter.
 The findings of this study indicate the need to distinguish between the "functionality" and the "necessity" of anger. Anger may silence the other person, increase tension in the situation, and prompt behavioral correction in the short term. However, the fact that anger functions does not mean that anger is indispensable. The observation that, within the same organization, warnings, responsibility confirmation, recurrence prevention, and error correction were achieved without using anger suggests that anger is not a necessary condition for workplace control.
 This study understands the difference between anger-based control and non-anger-based control not as a difference in individual personality, but as a difference in emotional currency, psychological safety, and effective cognitive repertoire. In workplaces where anger appears necessary, anger may function as a currency exchangeable for influence and legitimacy, and control methods other than anger may have become impoverished. On the other hand, in workplaces where non-anger-based control is established, low-intensity control resources such as explanation of reasons, calm warnings, laughter, and relationship maintenance are functioning. Therefore, what organizations should aim for is not to use anger more skillfully, but to design workplaces where necessary matters can be communicated, problems can be corrected, human relationships are not destroyed, and information continues to flow, even without using anger.

title: The Risk of Leading in Name Only: Values Camouflage©, Leadership, Governance and Mission Integrity in Corporations Especially in Purpose-Driven Organisations

detail.title: The Risk of Leading in Name Only: Values Camouflage©, Leadership, Governance and Mission Integrity in Corporations Especially in Purpose-Driven Organisations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Mission diminishment and creep which is the gradual dilution of an organisation's founding purpose or current strategic goals poses a defining challenge for mission-driven organisations navigating complex environments, leadership transitions, and the competing demands of contemporary governance. This paper reviews scholarship from organisational studies, personnel psychology, leadership theory, and nonprofit management to examine the mechanisms through which founding identity erodes and to identify the structural factors that protect against it. Central to the analysis is the phenomenon of values camouflage© , a term this paper introduces, where leaders adopt the language of organisational mission for employability, for cultural fit especially when they don't believe in what they are saying or to conceal real intent, without necessarily embodying the ethical, purposeful or relational commitments necessary to sustain that mission over time. At its most consequential, values camouflage does not merely compromise individual appointments or action, it recalibrates the normative environment of the entire organisation, quietly displacing founding purpose even integrity with the performed language and claims of mission until the two become indistinguishable from the outside and irreversible from within. Green washing is an example of this. Four interconnected domains of protective action are identified: engagement with modernity, recruitment integrity, the preservation of founding organisational purpose, and ongoing formation. Six evidence-based recommendations for boards, leaders, and mission stewards are offered. Limitations and future research opportunities are discussed.

title: Modular Recombination and Tacit Collusion: A Structural Threshold for Algorithmic Pricing in Bertrand Oligopoly
affiliations: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER) Bhopal

detail.title: Modular Recombination and Tacit Collusion: A Structural Threshold for Algorithmic Pricing in Bertrand Oligopoly
detail.abstract: We embed a genetic crossover operator into a differentiated Bertrand duopoly to model how firms dynamically recombine modular pricing strategies. Each firm's algorithm is encoded as a two-locus construct comprising a baseline margin module and a retaliation trigger module. The population of competing strategies is analyzed as a finite Markov chain whose transition probabilities are governed by the crossover rate P c. We demonstrate that the stability of tacit collusion depends critically on linkage disequilibrium between the two loci: a high crossover probability severs this linkage, endogenously generating Naïve Monopolist and Aggressive Defector phenotypes that precipitate Edgeworth cycles and dissolve the neutrally stable collusive attractor. Under the linear demand system, the critical threshold admits a closed-form solution, P * c = 1/2, which is invariant to all demand and cost parameters and corresponds exactly to the Folk Theorem critical discount factor for this model class. This universality carries a direct theoretical implication for antitrust policy: software architectures that structurally elevate P c above this threshold-through API interoperability mandates or open-source benchmarking-act as endogenous safeguards against autonomous algorithmic collusion, without requiring direct judicial intervention in observed price paths.

title: Beyond Trait Scores: A Framework for Contextual, Role-Specific Behavioural Assessment in High-Stakes People Decisions

detail.title: Beyond Trait Scores: A Framework for Contextual, Role-Specific Behavioural Assessment in High-Stakes People Decisions

detail.abstract: High-stakes people decisions now extend beyond hiring to promotion, redeployment, retention, and workforce restructuring, often under time pressure and growing governance scrutiny. Traditional psychometric instruments have made important contributions by standardising evidence about individual differences, but they were not primarily designed to produce role-specific, evidence-cited behavioural reasoning for live organisational decisions. This paper proposes the Contextual Behavioural Assessment Framework (CBAF), a conceptual and methodological framework that shifts the unit of analysis from trait description to situational behavioural inference. The framework integrates four design principles: career-stage calibration, role and environment contextualisation, scenario-based behavioural elicitation grounded in situational judgement test methodology, and cross-dimensional AI-supported inference. The paper reviews literature on personnel selection, situational judgement testing, trait psychometrics, AI in HR, algorithmic fairness, explainability, and auditability. It also distinguishes practice-informed conceptual development from formal empirical validation. The CBAF is presented as a responsible assessment architecture for making behavioural reasoning more relevant, transparent, consistent, and auditable while preserving human authority at the decision layer.

title: Human Resource Management Strategies and Economic Stability of Virtual Assistants: The Mediating Roles of Work Engagement and Job Autonomy and the Moderating Effect of Work-Life Balance

detail.title: Human Resource Management Strategies and Economic Stability of Virtual Assistants: The Mediating Roles of Work Engagement and Job Autonomy and the Moderating Effect of Work-Life Balance
detail.abstract: Despite the increasing significance of the role of virtual assistants in the digital economy, there is no empirical research that explores the interaction between HRM practices, job satisfaction, job autonomy, work engagement, work-life balance, and economic stability. The current research addresses these gaps by examining the linkage among variables and provides a full picture of the direct and indirect effect of HRM interventions on the job satisfaction and financial well-being using the motivation, autonomy and work-life balance. Quantitative research design was used, with 146 active virtual assistants selected using snowball sampling. The findings indicated that work engagement played a partial mediating role between the influence of HRM strategies on job satisfaction (axb=0.278, 38%, p<.001) and economic stability (axb=0.334, 34.5%, p<.001), which emphasizes the role of promoting employee energy, commitment, and absorption in remote work. Job autonomy was established as a weak mediator (axb=0.0410, 5.6%; axb=0.0882, 9.11%, p<.001), which shows that autonomy is a contributor to a smaller extent than the predominant role of HRM strategies. The work-life balance did not have any significant moderation effects on the tested relationships (p=0.589; p=0.806, ns), but it exhibited significant direct effects on employee outcomes, indicating that WLB should be regarded more as an independent predictor and contextual variable rather than a moderator. The results underscore the importance of HR policies that enhance autonomy, promote equitable and supportive HRM systems, and support work-life balance, while contributing to SDG 3, SDG 8, and SDG 10 through the promotion of healthy and inclusive remote work practices.

title: China Plus One：An Analysis of Taiwanese High-Tech industries FDI in China and Vietnam from the Perspectives of the Eclectic Paradigm and Technology Transfer
affiliations: National Yunlin University of Science and Technology, National Yunlin University of Science and Technology and National Yunlin University of Science and Technology

detail.title: China Plus One：An Analysis of Taiwanese High-Tech industries FDI in China and Vietnam from the Perspectives of the Eclectic Paradigm and Technology Transfer
detail.abstract: This study adopts a firm-level perspective, integrating the Eclectic Theory (OLI Paradigm) and technology transfer perspectives to establish a dynamic "OLI-TT" integrated framework. It examines the decision-making factors influencing FDI location choices in China and Vietnam for Taiwanese high-tech firms. A survey was administered to mid-level and senior managers from 168 Taiwanese parent companies with investments in China and Vietnam, utilizing a 7-point Likert scale. The research methodology involved first assessing the goodness-of-fit between the theoretical model and the collected data, followed by the application of conditional logistic analysis to empirically test 14 research hypotheses derived from the OLI framework and technology transfer theory.  The empirical results indicate：1. All hypotheses were statistically supported (p < .05), validating the explanatory power of the "OLI-TT" framework.2. Investment experience (OR = 2.91) and market factors (OR = 2.61) were the strongest facilitating factors, while cultural distance (OR = 0.33) and investment risk (OR = 0.35) were the strongest inhibiting factors.3. Technology performance variables explained 32.7% of the location decision variance (ΔR² = .327).4. The model demonstrated good fit (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p = .324), high overall explanatory power (Nagelkerke R² = .68), and statistical significance (χ² = 178.94, p < .001).  The research confirms that under the China Plus One strategy, Taiwanese firms simultaneously weigh traditional location-specific advantages and technology transfer performance, with risk aversion being a critical decision factor. This provides an important empirical foundation for investment theory in emerging economies.

title: Design and Optimization of an Intelligent Power Distribution Unit for Centralized Communication Power Supply Systems
affiliations: South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Design and Optimization of an Intelligent Power Distribution Unit for Centralized Communication Power Supply Systems
detail.abstract: Centralized communication power supply system sits at the heart of modern telecommunication infrastructure, yet the power distribution units (PDUs) that feed base stations, core switching rooms, and high-density server halls remain, for the most part, passive assemblies of copper and plastic. They switch, they fuse, and they log a handful of analogue readings; what they do not do is reason about what is happening downstream. This paper proposes an Intelligent Power Distribution Unit (IPDU) that combines edge-based deep learning, a digital-twin model, and a reinforcement-learning controller, so that the unit can forecast load, predict faults, reallocate branches, and coordinate with a cloud analytics layer in real time. A hybrid LSTM–Attention network is used for short-horizon load and thermal forecasting, while a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) agent, trained against a physics-based Simulink twin, drives the switching and routing decisions. We evaluate the design on a hardware-in-the-loop test-bed representative of a regional power distribution hub, benchmarking it against a conventional PDU and two published smart-PDU baselines. Across five operating scenarios, the IPDU reduces distribution losses by approximately 48% on average, cuts protection latency from around 30 ms to under 4 ms, lifts service availability from 99.72% to 99.983%, and detects incipient faults with an AUC of 0.982. The framework scales to 512 managed branches with a median decision time below 13 ms, and a 30-day field pilot at three sites confirms the simulation results within 2.4% relative error. Our results indicate that a tightly coupled learning controller is a practical path towards more reliable, lower-loss, and more observable communication power infrastructure. The reported figures pertain to the described HIL test-bed, a 16-branch IPDU prototype, and a 30-day three-site field pilot; broader multi-site and multi-climate deployments, as well as side-by-side comparisons against recent transformer-based and graph-neural-network-based energy-management frameworks, are identified as required next steps before the reported gains can be claimed as universally generalizable.

title: Impact of Local Flexibility Market Design on the Optimal Provision of Balancing Services in Multi-Energy Microgrids​
affiliations: Polytechnic University of Milan, Polytechnic University of Milan and Polytechnic University of Milan

detail.title: Impact of Local Flexibility Market Design on the Optimal Provision of Balancing Services in Multi-Energy Microgrids​
detail.abstract: The increasing penetration of distributed energy resources and end-use electrification are making flexibility a key resource for distribution system operators. Local flexibility markets are emerging as a promising mechanism, but their economic attractiveness for balancing service providers remains uncertain. This paper quantifies the realistic economic value that an aggregation of distributed energy resources can obtain by participating in a local flexibility market, while explicitly accounting for the interaction with implicit flexibility, driven by electricity-bill optimization. The analysis focuses on PoliGrid, the multi-energy microgrid of Politecnico di Milano, participating in MiNDFlex, the local flexibility market developed by Unareti. A block-based mixed-integer linear programming framework is used to optimize PoliGrid operation over a full year. The scheduling stage determines the optimal upward power bands to be offered in the monthly auctions. The operation stage simulates real system performance through a rolling-horizon approach, considering forecast errors and service activation orders. The study compares configurations with and without a 2 MW/4 MWh BESS and evaluates alternative market design choices. Results show that, without storage, market participation is never economically convenient. Conversely, with a BESS, annual savings increase from about 43 k€/year under implicit flexibility alone to about 148 k€/year when implicit and explicit flexibility are combined. Sensitivity analyses highlight the importance of baseline selection, the operational challenges associated with capacity-limitation products, and the benefits of shorter auction horizons and more granular daily products. These findings highlight the role of storage in unlocking LFM revenues and the strong impact of market design on flexibility value.

title: The Tri-Layer Integrated Model Revised: A Four-Layer Framework for Recursive Classification

detail.title: The Tri-Layer Integrated Model Revised: A Four-Layer Framework for Recursive Classification
detail.abstract: This paper establishes the canonical four-layer form of the Tri-Layer Integrated Model (TLIM), a framework for analyzing how classification systems generate and sustain recursive institutional processes. The revised model adds a foundational layer-L0 Cultural Repertoire-to the original three-layer structure, and formalizes the recursive feedback loop through which governed environments reshape the cultural materials from which future classifications are drawn. TLIM proposes that classification does not merely describe futures; it structures the predictive environments through which futures become governable. The four layers-Cultural Repertoire, Classification, Predictive Governance, and Causal Environment-form a closed cycle of institutional meaning-production in which narratives become categories, categories become forecasts, forecasts become institutional conditions, and those conditions replenish the repertoire. The paper further addresses the phenomenon of infrastructure self-reading, in which AI systems, markets, media platforms, and policy institutions increasingly ingest one another's outputs, and identifies geopolitical toolkit divergence as a structural feature of the model's application. This short paper serves as a canonical anchor for subsequent applications of TLIM across regulatory, security, media, and knowledge-governance domains.

title: Warning-guided hydrogen energy storage management for reliable operation of wind-PV-hydrogen multi-energy systems
affiliations: Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University and Zhengzhou University

detail.title: Warning-guided hydrogen energy storage management for reliable operation of wind-PV-hydrogen multi-energy systems
detail.abstract: Hydrogen energy storage (HES) is essential for reliable operation of wind-PV-hydrogen multi-energy systems, but renewable fluctuation and seasonal mismatch may deplete storage reserves before high-risk power-deficit periods. To address this issue, this paper proposes a warning-guided HES management framework that converts operating-state information into adaptive charging and discharging decisions. The framework first models the wind-PV direct supply path, electric-to-hydrogen conversion path, and hydrogen-to-power support path to characterize reserve dynamics and loss-of-load risk. Forward-looking reserve-warning signals are then extracted from unlabeled multi-source measurements: daily features are constructed from hourly data, unsupervised clustering is used to discover physically interpretable operating states, and a two-stage ensemble model estimates state probabilities. A cost-sensitive health index, weighted rolling moving average model, and sliding-window dynamic threshold are further used to generate reserve warnings. Based on these warnings, an adaptive scheduling strategy adjusts electrolyzer charging and fuel-cell discharging to preserve storage reserves and support power-deficit periods. Validation using measured data from the Rye microgrid in Norway shows that the proposed method achieves 97.67% pseudo-label-based operating-state recognition accuracy, reduces cumulative loss of load by 8.84%, increases the average HES state of charge by 6.30 percentage points, and decreases the power-supply failure transition probability by 21.94%. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework improves reliable operation by coordinating electric-to-hydrogen reserve preparation and hydrogen-to-power support under warning conditions.

title: From Nudge to Retention: How Interface Design Interventions Reduce App Hopping Behaviour Through Perceived Task Efficiency
affiliations: , SVKM's NMIMS Deemed to be University - Narsee Monjee Institute of Management Studies, Jiwaji University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: From Nudge to Retention: How Interface Design Interventions Reduce App Hopping Behaviour Through Perceived Task Efficiency
detail.abstract: Purpose This study examines how three types of behavioural nudges — progress feedback nudges, continuity nudges, and attention/friction nudges affects app hopping behaviour in mobile application environments. It further explores perceived task efficiency as a mediating mechanism linking these nudges to app switching behaviour.MethodologyA quantitative cross-sectional survey was administered online to smartphone users who regularly engage with multiple mobile applications. Partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) was used for data analysis.Findings All three nudge types — progress feedback, default continuity, and attention/friction — significantly reduce app hopping behaviour and positively enhance perceived task efficiency. Perceived task efficiency emerges as a strong and significant mediator across all three nudge-to-app-hopping paths. The model explains 56.7% of the variance in app hopping behaviour (R² = 0.567) and 47.2% in perceived task efficiency (R² = 0.472). All hypotheses (H1 to H6) are supported at p < 0.001.Implications Mobile application designers and UX practitioners should integrate default continuity features (e.g., in-app task completion, auto-save), progress feedback mechanisms (e.g., completion bars), and light-touch friction cues (e.g., confirmation prompts before exit) to enhance user retention, reduce disruptive app switching, and improve overall user experience.Originality /value This study is one of the first attempt to combine theory of nudge with already established information systems models (UTAUT2) in the context of mobile app switching. It proposes perceived task efficiency as a new intermediate variable between the nudge design of an interface and behaviour (app switching), providing a theoretically supported and practically applicable model.

title: Stabilizing Token-Mediated Marketplaces through Closed-Loop Reserve Funds and Dynamic Supply Locking
affiliations: Hanoi University of Science and Technology and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Stabilizing Token-Mediated Marketplaces through Closed-Loop Reserve Funds and Dynamic Supply Locking
detail.abstract: Token-mediated digital marketplaces increasingly use native tokens as payment, incentive, liquidity, and governance instruments. In these environments, token-price instability is not merely a speculative financial risk: it can affect service affordability, supplier reward value, liquidity participation, treasury capacity, and platform trust. This paper studies native-token instability as a transaction-infrastructure risk and proposes a closed-loop Stabilization Reserve Fund (SRF) as a cost-aware marketplace-governance mechanism. The SRF combines reserve-funded feedback intervention, volatility-triggered locking of eligible supply, intervention safeguards, and a dynamic reserve-refilling transaction tax. Unlike algorithmic peg mechanisms, it does not target a fixed price. Instead, it aims to dampen short-horizon downside stress while preserving long-run market price discovery. We evaluate the SRF through engineered crash simulations, controller ablations, Burn-and-Mint-Equilibrium regime stress tests, historical token-panel replay, eligible-supply sensitivity analysis, and explicit economic cost accounting. To connect token-market stabilization with electronic-commerce outcomes, we further translate price-path effects into marketplace-facing proxy indices for service affordability, supplier reward purchasing power, treasury intervention burden, and liquidity-access burden. In the benchmark engineered-crash setting with the upper-bound eligible-supply configuration (θ = 1.00), the Full SRF reduces rolling 14-day drawdown by 17.6%, worst one-day loss by 18.6%, and global maximum drawdown by 22.5% relative to no intervention. Under a more practical partial opt-in configuration (θ = 0.50), rolling drawdown reduction remains 11.8%. The results indicate that SRF is best understood not as a universal solution to token volatility, but as a tunable governance instrument for token-mediated marketplaces. Its benefits arise from improved short-horizon downside protection and reserve management, while its costs appear through transaction taxation, temporary liquidity restrictions, reserve utilization, intervention turnover, and price-discovery distortion. The paper contributes a decision framework for marketplace operators to evaluate when stabilization benefits justify user-facing governance costs.

title: From Volume to Identity: Identity-based Forestry and the Future of High-resolution Environmental Governance

detail.title: From Volume to Identity: Identity-based Forestry and the Future of High-resolution Environmental Governance

detail.abstract:
Illegal timber laundering persists globally despite advances in satellite monitoring, certification systems, and increasingly sophisticated forest governance architectures. This paper argues that the persistence of illegal forest extraction is not explained solely by weak enforcement, corruption, or insufficient monitoring technologies, but also by a structural limitation embedded within contemporary forest governance itself. Current systems remain predominantly organized around volumetric abstraction, in which forests are regulated through aggregated inventories, authorized balances, and statistical reconciliation mechanisms rather than through persistent ecological identity continuity.
The paper introduces the concept of Identity Collapse to describe the progressive loss of verifiable biological linkage when individual trees are transformed into fungible volumetric units across extraction, transportation, industrial processing, commercialization, and environmental accounting systems. Under such conditions, timber legality increasingly depends on documentary compatibility and statistical coherence rather than on persistent ecological verification, creating structural conditions that facilitate substitution, laundering, and ecological anonymity within legal supply chains.
In response, this paper proposes a transition from volume-based forestry toward Identity-Based Forestry, operationalized through the proposed Tree-Level Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (TLMRV) framework. TLMRV is conceptualized as an interoperable ecological identity architecture designed to preserve verifiable linkage between biological origin, material flow, carbon accounting, and regulatory verification systems throughout the forest governance lifecycle.
The paper further argues that the implications of identity-based governance extend beyond timber legality into broader domains of climate governance, carbon integrity, ESG accountability, biodiversity verification, environmental due diligence, and high-resolution environmental governance systems. As climate economies become increasingly data-intensive, environmental trust may progressively depend on stronger forms of ecological continuity, permanence verification, traceability persistence, and auditable environmental authenticity.
Ultimately, this paper argues that the future credibility of forest governance may depend not only on improving environmental measurement accuracy, but on preserving the continuity of the ecological identities from which environmental value itself emerges.

title: A Rule-Based Borrower Screening Framework for Digital Agricultural Lending: A Case Study of Remote Credit Decisioning in Kazakhstan

detail.title: A Rule-Based Borrower Screening Framework for Digital Agricultural Lending: A Case Study of Remote Credit Decisioning in Kazakhstan

detail.abstract: This paper presents a case study of a rule-based borrower screening framework used in digital agricultural lending in Kazakhstan. The project was developed in collaboration with Agrarian Credit Corporation and focused on a real pre-screening system integrated into the Agrocredit mobile application and web portal. The system supports remote preliminary credit decisioning for agricultural producers by checking whether an application can move forward to the next stage of review. Unlike score-based models that use weighted coefficients, probability estimates, or risk bands, the framework described here follows a deterministic pass/fail logic. It uses rule-based conditions to process financial, legal, and registry-based information and convert these inputs into a structured preliminary classification result. The system does not make a final lending decision. Instead, it performs an early-stage screening step that either allows the application to proceed or blocks it until the detected issues are resolved. The paper explains the model's structure, the main categories of screening factors, the data sources used, and the practical decision logic implemented in the process. It also describes measurable operational results. According to the implementation context discussed here, preliminary screening that previously could take up to 15 days in an office-based process can now be completed automatically in about 2-5 minutes in the online channel. Initial documentation requirements have also been reduced, and approximately 80-90% of applications can be checked automatically at the pre-screening stage. The case is relevant not only for digital finance but also for applied mathematics in finance, because it shows how heterogeneous borrower-related variables can be formalized into a deterministic decision framework for real financial use.

title: Data-driven Decision Making and Sales Growth In FMCG Companies In Bangladesh: A Conceptual Review And Research Agenda
affiliations: East West University and North South University

detail.title: Data-driven Decision Making and Sales Growth In FMCG Companies In Bangladesh: A Conceptual Review And Research Agenda
detail.abstract: This paper examines how data-driven decision making can support sales growth in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies in Bangladesh. The manuscript is positioned as a conceptual review article rather than an empirical study. It synthesizes research on analytics capability, retail analytics, demand forecasting, promotion optimization, distribution execution, and organizational readiness, then interprets these insights in the context of Bangladesh's FMCG market. The review suggests that data-driven decision making affects sales growth through four linked mechanisms: stronger customer insight, better demand forecasting, more effective promotion decisions, and tighter distribution execution. The paper also argues that the sales effect of data is conditional rather than automatic. Data quality, managerial commitment, employee capability, and an analytical culture shape whether data is translated into timely commercial action. The article contributes in three ways. First, it consolidates fragmented literature into one Bangladesh-relevant framework. Second, it explains why the FMCG context requires fast, outlet-level, evidence-based decisions. Third, it proposes a research agenda for future empirical work in Bangladesh. The paper concludes that FMCG firms can improve sales growth when they move beyond routine reporting and use data as a decision infrastructure across forecasting, promotion, and route-to-market management.

title: Trust equilibrium theory
affiliations: Edith Cowan University

detail.title: Trust equilibrium theory
detail.abstract: Online payment security is designed to mitigate fraudulent transaction, yet hyper-engineered security parameters routinely introduce user experience friction, that precipitates shopping cart abandonment at the payment stage. This study draws upon the microeconomic foundations of demand and supply equilibrium to conceptualise and test "Trust Equilibrium Theory". The theory examines the trade-offs between transaction security, user convenience, and consumer trust. This study implements an experimental simulation which models real-time online checkout behaviours across multiple security thresholds. We apply survival analysis, specifically Kaplan-Meier estimators and Cox proportional hazards regressions, to evaluate the time-to-event dynamics of transaction abandonment. Our results reveal an intricate relationship. While standalone security increments can suppress conversions, the interaction effect between trust signals and transaction convenience significantly buffers attrition, yielding a 26% reduction in abandonment risk. Crucially, we identify a counter-intuitive behaviour among digitally proficient users, who exhibit a significantly higher rate of transaction abandonment when subject to redundant security protocols. These findings offer actionable empirical frameworks for platform architects and e-commerce merchants to dynamically optimise security architectures without increasing transaction attrition rate.​

detail.abstract:
OpenAPI specifications have become foundational for documenting and consuming REST
APIs, but large organizations still face significant friction when they try to scale those integrations
across many teams and services. Developers must retrieve and interpret specification files, generate
client code, configure authentication and retries, manage versioning, and keep implementations
aligned across distributed environments. This technical-report edition describes Orion Link,
a federated OpenAPI client gateway and managed hosted service designed to centralize those
tasks. Orion Link automates generated-client management, configuration, version transitions,
monitoring, and plug-and-play extensibility, while also supporting a sidecar model for lower-
latency paths. The article argues that a federated, centrally governed client layer can reduce
repetitive boilerplate, improve consistency, and simplify API consumption at enterprise scale.

title: A Digital Twin-Based Adaptive Optimization Framework for LNG Processes under Equipment Degradation
affiliations: Inha University, Inha University and Inha University

detail.title: A Digital Twin-Based Adaptive Optimization Framework for LNG Processes under Equipment Degradation
detail.abstract: The energy consumption of LNG liquefaction processes is strongly affected by coupled refrigerant compression, cryogenic heat exchange, expansion, recirculation, feed conditions, operating variables, and equipment performance. Therefore, an optimization framework is required that can update operating decisions as process conditions change and maintain model reliability under equipment degradation. This study proposes a degradation-aware digital twin-based AI optimization framework that collects process-consistent data from the digital twin, uses an ML surrogate model to propose optimal operating conditions, and updates the model under degradation. The calibrated digital twin, constructed using actual LNG operating data, reduced the average prediction error of key process variables from 3.24% to 0.78% and served as a reference environment for data generation and revalidation of optimized operating conditions. To maintain optimization applicability under process changes, the pretrained surrogate model was updated using limited degraded-process data through a layer-wise transfer learning strategy designed to preserve prediction accuracy and generalization performance. The updated surrogate model was evaluated on unseen degraded-process data and at optimized operating points reintroduced into the digital twin, verifying its reliability under changing operating and degradation scenarios. Finally, energy consumption was compared to assess process-level effectiveness. Compared with the existing operating strategy, the proposed framework achieved average energy savings of 1.51%, 1.66%, and 3.19% under normal, uniformly degraded, and locally degraded conditions, respectively. Under degradation, model updating provided additional savings of 1.12% and 3.76% compared with optimization using the non-updated surrogate model.

title: AI-Agent Framework for Sales Risk Identification and Response in Live-Commerce Environments
affiliations: , Chung-Ang University, Chung-Ang University, GS Retail Co. Ltd and Korea University

detail.title: AI-Agent Framework for Sales Risk Identification and Response in Live-Commerce Environments
detail.abstract: Conventional rule-based approaches are widely used for analyzing customer evaluations in e-commerce and live-commerce environments. However, these approaches often show limitations in detecting newly emerging product issues and prioritizing business-critical risks. To address these limitations, this study proposes an intelligent AI-agent framework for proactive product-risk identification and sales-response support. First, semantic embeddings generated using Sentence-Transformers are integrated with the HDBSCAN clustering algorithm to identify latent issue patterns and remove noisy evaluations. Subsequently, class-based term frequency-inverse document frequency is employed to extract representative keywords from clustered customer feedback. Based on the extracted information, the Llama large language model automatically generates product defect categories and issue descriptions. In addition, this study introduces a risk-scoring mechanism incorporating vote-related metadata to identify defect issues with high customer churn potential. The most influential defect category is further analyzed using aspect-level sentiment analysis to derive fine-grained customer sentiment patterns. Finally, the proposed framework automatically generates objection-response guidelines that can be directly utilized in live-commerce broadcasting and customer-response operations. The proposed framework demonstrates how large language models can be integrated into an automated decision-support architecture for proactive risk management in e-commerce environments.

title: From AI experimentation to operational capability: Governance routines and platform architectures for AI-first organizations
affiliations: Purdue University

detail.title: From AI experimentation to operational capability: Governance routines and platform architectures for AI-first organizations
detail.abstract: We develop the Sustained Alignment Framework (SAF), a governance-centered account of why artificial intelligence initiatives often fail to move from successful pilots to durable operational capability. Drawing on dynamic capabilities, strategic intelligence, and digital transformation literatures, we argue that failure is primarily organizational rather than technical. Analytic capability generates strategic value only when interpreted, evaluated, and institutionalized through coherent governance structures. SAF operationalizes AI strategy alignment through strategic fit, evaluative coherence, and durable value realization, while positioning the Strategic Intelligence Capability Stack (AI-SI-DT) as the architecture sustaining these dimensions across large-scale industrial platform enterprises and archival case-based research.

title: Onboard autonomous mission planning: synergies and challenges of deep reinforcement learning and neural multi-objective optimization

detail.title: Onboard autonomous mission planning: synergies and challenges of deep reinforcement learning and neural multi-objective optimization
detail.abstract: The rapid growth of satellite constellations and space debris challenges traditional manual control. Onboard autonomous mission planning, powered by Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) and Neural Multi-Objective Optimization (NMOO), offers a promising solution. DRL enables real-time decisions in dynamic environments, while NMOO balances conflicting goals like task priority and energy use. Despite significant progress, challenges remain in computational complexity, data quality, and real-time demands. This paper reviews recent advances, analyzes key challenges, and outlines future directions.

title: Hub location–routing under demand uncertainty: A vertical integration perspective in maritime transportation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Nottingham and Nottingham University Business School

detail.title: Hub location–routing under demand uncertainty: A vertical integration perspective in maritime transportation
detail.abstract: Demand uncertainty plays a crucial role in hub location decisions since hub facilities represent long-term infrastructure investments. This paper studies a hub location–routing problem under demand uncertainty, motivated by the growing involvement of shipping lines in container terminal operations within maritime supply chains. The problem is formulated as a possibilistic mixed-integer linear program with imprecise origin–destination demands and transformed into an auxiliary crisp counterpart using a fuzzy measure-based chance constrained programming approach. To efficiently solve large-scale instances, we develop a Tabu Search algorithm and a decomposition heuristic that iteratively addresses three interrelated subproblems. Computational experiments based on real-world data from major Mediterranean container terminals demonstrate that the proposed methods obtain optimal or near-optimal solutions for instances with up to 56 nodes. The results also show that demand uncertainty can substantially influence hub investment decisions, network configuration, and total costs, highlighting the importance of explicitly incorporating uncertainty into strategic hub-and-spoke network design in maritime transportation systems.
