detail.abstract:
AML transaction monitoring systems are widely deployed across financial institutions, yet they often remain difficult to reconstruct, explain, and evaluate in production. This paper argues that a key limitation is not only insufficient detection logic, but insufficient system observability. It defines AML Observability as the capability to reconstruct detection-relevant decisions across the full processing lifecycle and reframes recurring AML control breakdowns as diagnosability gaps rather than isolated detection misses.

The paper makes five linked contributions. First, it proposes a five-layer AML observability architecture and the Transformation Spiral as a sequencing model linking data governance, system observability, AI observability, and AI enablement. Second, it interprets public enforcement cases through an OBASHI-informed lens and derives a compact anti-pattern library, including Upstream Blindspot, Silent Transformation Drop, Threshold Suppression, and Broken Feedback Loop. Third, it formalizes a minimal event-centric proof of concept in Python built around an AMLTrace/AMLTraceEvent model, explicit query semantics for why_flagged, why_not_flagged, and what_changed, and privacy-aware trace retention. Fourth, it extends the same trace schema toward AI governance by embedding model-specific artifacts such as feature attribution, confidence distributions, and drift indicators into the compliance trace. Fifth, it adds a production-oriented architecture sketch and a larger synthetic comparison between a monitoring-only baseline and an observable system.

The larger evaluation processes 1,000 synthetic transactions, including 300 injected faults distributed across six fault families spanning the five-layer stack. Across the fault cases, the observable system improves mean diagnosis completeness from 0.25 to 1.00, failure-layer attribution accuracy from 0.17 to 1.00, and reduces explanation steps from 4.0 to 1.0 relative to the baseline. A sizing model based on the current PoC event structure further indicates an average raw telemetry footprint of roughly 3.38 GB per one million transactions, falling to about 2.05 GB under the selective retention policy. These results remain synthetic and do not constitute production validation, but they provide stronger empirical and engineering support for the claim that observability improves diagnosability in AML systems.

The paper situates these results explicitly within the regulatory anchoring provided by BCBS 239 on risk-data aggregation and the European Central Bank's 2024 guide on effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting, both of which identify attribute-level data lineage as a top-priority supervisory expectation. The AMLTrace model presented here operationalizes that expectation for the AML pipeline. The paper also positions itself against the rapidly growing literature on AI auditability: where that literature asks whether AI outputs can be audited, this paper argues that the architectural precondition for auditability is system-level observability across the full processing lifecycle. Observability is therefore neither a substitute for governance nor an alternative to AI, but the architectural condition under which governance becomes evidence-based and AI becomes more governable.

title: An investigation into the use of working-day length flexibility for controlling production unit workload and lead time performance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: An investigation into the use of working-day length flexibility for controlling production unit workload and lead time performance
detail.abstract: Many production units exhibit high variability in order flow times, primarily due to variations in processing and arrival times, resulting in substantial variability in the workload at workstations. Obviously, reducing the variations in workload will result in reduced flow time variability, enabling shorter and more reliable lead times at the supply chain level. We present an analytically derived rule for setting the daily working time per workstation such that the average flow time of the orders present at a workstation is close to a target flow time. We test its performance for a single workstation and a five-workstation production unit, with daily working time per workstation ranging from 7 to 9 hours. We show that, for order arrival rates corresponding to 85%, 90%, and 95% capacity utilization under a fixed daily working time, our flexible working-time workload control rule yields a much lower flow-time distribution than under fixed daily working time. This allows quoting much shorter lead times for a given level of delivery reliability.,Our workload control rule adapts the deployed operator capacity to the capacity required by incoming orders. As a result, the production unit can cope with some uncertainty in the order arrival rate. We show that for a difference of up to 5% between actual and expected arrival rate, the order flow time distributions are quite close to each other. This allows the production unit to quote short, reliable lead times despite uncertainty in the order arrival rate.

title: Higher Education Student Perceptions Toward Extended Reality (XR) in Global Competence Era: A Pilot Study
affiliations: , Universiti Malaysia Sarawak and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Higher Education Student Perceptions Toward Extended Reality (XR) in Global Competence Era: A Pilot Study
detail.abstract: Virtual reality (VR), augmented reality (AR), and mixed reality (MR) are all parts of extended reality (XR), which has become a game-changing technological advancement in higher education. XR technologies provide interactive and immersive learning environments that may improve global competency development, experiential learning, and student engagement. Higher education courses are increasingly emphasizing global competence, which includes the capacity to comprehend global challenges, value cultural variety, and act responsibly in a globalized environment. Due to the growing interest in XR, few studies have looked at students' preparedness and attitudes for the integration of XR in relation to global competence and global citizenship education (GCED). In this pilot study, undergraduate students (N=30) from education, arts and humanities, and social sciences programs in two Malaysian public universities participated to share their perceptions on the topic. Students' awareness of XR technologies, technological readiness, perceived utility, and perceptions on XR for global competence were all assessed using an online survey questionnaire. According to descriptive research, students' perceptions of XR technologies' educational potential were generally positive, especially to improve engagement, experiential learning, and cross-cultural understanding. However, lack of prior experience and restricted access to XR tools were noted as possible obstacles. In addition to highlighting the necessity of institutional support, training, and infrastructure to enable successful XR integration in higher education, the findings offer initial insights into students' preparedness for immersive technologies.

title: When Leaders Leave Without Warning: A Relational Typology of Employee Sensemaking Under Abrupt Leadership Exits
affiliations: Australian Catholic University (ACU), University of Queensland, Monash University, Keele University - Keele Business School and University of Ilorin

detail.title: When Leaders Leave Without Warning: A Relational Typology of Employee Sensemaking Under Abrupt Leadership Exits
detail.abstract: Purpose-This study examines how employees interpret and emotionally respond to abrupt and poorly communicated leadership exits in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). While leadership succession research has focused largely on planned transitions and firm-level outcomes, less is known about how sudden departures shape employee sensemaking and why reactions vary in intensity. We investigate how relational proximity to the departed leader and perceived procedural legitimacy condition employees' interpretive responses, and under what circumstances abrupt exits escalate from routine organisational change to identitylevel disruption. Design/methodology/approach-The study employs a qualitative, interpretivist design, based on 24 semistructured interviews with employees across eight Australian SMEs. Data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify patterned configurations of meaning-making. The analysis yielded a typology of four interpretive responses, structured by relational proximity and perceived threat intensity. Findings-The findings identify four patterned responses to abrupt leadership exits: Business as Usual, Job Insecurity, Disaster and Existential Threat. These responses reflect distinct combinations of emotional intensity, relational proximity and legitimacy perceptions. Rather than unfolding as sequential stages, responses represent qualitatively different interpretive positions. High relational proximity and low perceived procedural legitimacy were associated with escalated interpretations, including organisational crisis framing and identity-level disruption. Originality/value-This study advances change management research by conceptualising abrupt leadership exits as relationally structured interpretive events. It introduces a typology that specifies boundary conditions under which emotional reactions escalate into organisational crisis or identity rupture. By integrating sensemaking, procedural legitimacy and identity perspectives, the study contributes a relationally contingent model of employee responses to sudden leadership change.

title: How Visitor Satisfaction and Intention to Revisit Are Created by Event Quality and Perceived Value? A Lesson at the Local Food Festival in Brebes
affiliations: , Universitas Pejuang Republik  and Unaffiliated Author

detail.title: How Visitor Satisfaction and Intention to Revisit Are Created by Event Quality and Perceived Value? A Lesson at the Local Food Festival in Brebes
detail.abstract: The emergence of many festivals and events shows that Arranging festivals centered around specific themes has the potential to boost economic development on both local and national scales. To investigate how events can improve visitors' perception of event quality, perceived value, trust, visitor satisfaction, and behavioral intentions, the annual food festival during the 344th anniversary celebration of Brebes was selected to explore these relationships. A total of 350 questionnaires were distributed to visitors and the data analysis was performed on 335 valid questionnaires using structural equation modeling. The results show that event quality has a positive and significant effect on perceived value (β = 0.205; p-value 0.037 <0.05). In addition, perceived value has a positive and significant effect on trust (β = 0.0585; p-value 0.000 <0.05). Finally, trust has a positive impact on event satisfaction (p-value 0.000 <0.05), which in turn affects the intention to revisit (p-value 0.004 <0.05). Drawing from these observed outcomes, this research provides practical and theoretical insights for event management entities and festival organizers to continue hosting annual theme-centered festivals during specific occasions and destinations to improve visitors' attachment to the values and authenticity offered.

title: " The Al-Jahizian Model: An Arab-Heritage Framework for Interpreting Human-AI Epistemic Interaction

detail.title: " The Al-Jahizian Model: An Arab-Heritage Framework for Interpreting Human-AI Epistemic Interaction

contentType.other: From the Debate of the Rooster and the Dog to a Theory of Balanced Digital Dialogue .

detail.abstract: Contemporary studies of Artificial Intelligence face a crisis in their dominant analytical paradigm, the "Turing Test." This paper aims to critique this test, which focuses superficially on simulation, and to propose an alternative framework inspired by Arab intellectual heritage. The paper introduces the "Al-Jahizian Model," derived from "The Debate of the Rooster and the Dog," as a model centered on "functional argumentative contestation" (al-tadāfuʿ al-ḥijājī al-waẓīfī) as a mechanism for knowledge production. The paper argues that this model transcends current "Human AI Collaboration" research by offering a normative philosophical framework aimed at achieving "epistemic balance" rather than mere "interactive efficiency." Through a comparative analytical method, and using a tripartite dialogue (human, generative AI, and critical AI) as a case study, the research arrives at the "Theory of Dialogue Collapse," which identifies three potential pathological scenarios when one of the model's pillars is absent. The paper concludes that the human role transcends that of a "user" to become the "wise coordinator" (Phronesis) who endows digital dialogue with its purpose (Telos) and value. Finally, it proposes a design framework for developing future balanced dialogue systems.

title: Organizational Dynamics and Strategic Management Practices in Deposit Money Banks
affiliations: and Ignatius Ajuru University of Education

detail.title: Organizational Dynamics and Strategic Management Practices in Deposit Money Banks
detail.abstract: This study examined the effect of organizational dynamics on strategic management practices in deposit money banks. The business environment in which organizations operate is dynamic and turbulent with constant and face pace changes that render yester-years irrelevant. While the specific objectives of the study were: to examine the effect of organizational culture on innovation strategy in deposit money banks, to examine the effect of organizational culture on information sharing practice in deposit money banks, to examine the effect of organizational learning on innovation strategy in deposit money banks, and to examine the effect of organizational learning on information sharing practice in deposit money banks. This study anchored on The Theory of the Learning Organization. In conclusion, organizational dynamics are essential to meeting the needs of technology adoption since they improve productivity and prevent time wastage. The study recommends that, every bank should assess its strategy annually to determine whether it aligns with its objectives, and strategic evaluation need to be constant rather than occasional.

title: Human Authenticity as Economic Value Under Generative Abundance
affiliations: Apna.Co

detail.title: Human Authenticity as Economic Value Under Generative Abundance
detail.abstract: When imitation is free, authenticity becomes expensive. Generative AI lowers the cost of producing high-quality synthetic goods, threatening human producers. But this substitution assumes consumers only care about functional quality. We model a market where human origin enters the utility function directly. As synthetic outputs flood the market, verified human provenance becomes a scarce, valuable attribute. The market bifurcates: a low-price synthetic commodity tier and a high-price verified-human tier. Human producers survive not by competing on quality or price, but by selling verifiable authenticity. The future premium is on proving you are human.

title: Corporate Responses to the Logics of Space Mining: The Case of ispace Inc
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Corporate Responses to the Logics of Space Mining: The Case of ispace Inc
detail.abstract: Following an institutional logics perspective, this paper explores how one of the most prominent corporations – the Japanese start-up firm ispace Inc – inhabiting the field of space mining has responded to the logics that govern this field. Examining the prevalence of such logics in the company’s extensive news communication, we find that its responses are dominated by the entrepreneurial logic that has grown increasingly prominent in this field. By contrast, evidence of the sustainability logic, that has emerged as a counter-reaction to the entrepreneurial logic, is sparser but increasing over time. A third, regulatory logic also features in the company’s news communication and has mediated the entrepreneurial and sustainability logics in a way that has pulled the latter logics apart and reinforced a state of logics segregation. Taken together, our findings reinforce emerging concerns that the entrepreneurial logic is overshadowing the sustainability logic and that the two logics may be difficult to reconcile in the field of space mining. We discuss the implications of our findings for policy development and future research.

title: Efficient Equalization Strategies for Dynamic Reconfigurable Battery Systems-revised
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University, Tsinghua University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Efficient Equalization Strategies for Dynamic Reconfigurable Battery Systems-revised
detail.abstract: Based on dynamic reconfigurable technology, an efficient battery system equalization method is proposed. In the case of series equalization, SOC and SOH matrices of the battery system are established, and a state space matrix is formed. Considering the probability distribution of parameters and the required number of control switches, the optimal series equalization path is obtained. In terms of parallel equalization, the staged charging and discharging strategy is adopted, and the SOH of the battery module is considered to achieve system online parallel equalization and optimized operation during faults; furthermore, taking into account the losses of the battery and MOSFET, the controllable self-equalization strategy during static state and the controllable online equalization strategy during operation at the battery module level are established to achieve multi-objective optimization control, which can improve the overall consistency and available capacity of the battery system.

title: Fine-Grained Load Distribution of Cascade Hydropower Stations Considering Vibration-Zone Crossings: A Spatiotemporal Hierarchical Decoupling Framework
affiliations: Hohai University, Zhejiang University, Tsinghua University and Hohai University

detail.title: Fine-Grained Load Distribution of Cascade Hydropower Stations Considering Vibration-Zone Crossings: A Spatiotemporal Hierarchical Decoupling Framework
detail.abstract: The large-scale integration of renewables has intensified the peak-shaving duties of hydropower stations, making frequent unit startup/shutdown operations and vibration-zone (VZ) crossings increasingly prominent challenges. To achieve fine-grained load distribution while ensuring dispatch reliability, the startup/shutdown count and the VZ-crossing count must be incorporated alongside the conventional economic operation objective. However, their inclusion causes an explosive growth in unit-level integer variables. The cascade hydraulic coupling and the unit-level nonlinearities further add to the modelling difficulty, rendering the conventional “station-unit” two-layer nested framework unable to balance solution efficiency and quality. To this end, a spatiotemporal hierarchical decoupling framework is proposed for fine-grained load distribution of cascade hydropower stations, decomposing the problem into three coupled sub-problems: inter-station load distribution, unit commitment, and intra-station fine-grained dispatch. Spatially, the inter-station and intra-station distributions are decoupled so that each layer addresses either the hydraulic coupling or the unit-level nonlinearities, but not both. Temporally, the intra-station layer is split into hourly unit commitment and 15-minute fine-grained dispatch, with each sub-problem solved at its native temporal scale and globally coordinated through closed-loop feedback of the water consumption coefficient. A case study on the Hongjiadu-Dongfeng-Suofengying cascade of the Wujiang River shows that, the proposed three-objective model reduces VZ crossings by 59% and 76%, respectively, relative to the single- and dual-objective models, at an additional water-energy cost of only 1% and without additional startup/shutdown operations. Compared with the conventional two-layer nested framework, the proposed framework cuts the solve time from 847 s to 18 s, achieving an approximately 47-fold speedup while preserving solution quality.

title: Two-stage optimization of electric vehicle aggregators via a scalable multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework with physics-constrained action repair
affiliations: South China University of Technology, South China University of Technology and South China University of Technology

detail.title: Two-stage optimization of electric vehicle aggregators via a scalable multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework with physics-constrained action repair
detail.abstract: The disorderly charging of large-scale electric vehicles (EVs) poses challenges to the stable operation of distribution networks, while their adjustable flexibility provides potential for EV aggregators (EVAs) to participate in multi-market operations. The optimal management of large-scale EVs is a high-dimensional, strongly stochastic, and multi-strictly constrained sequential decision problem. The traditional decoupling methods often struggle to maintain scheduling accuracy when dealing with highly uncertain operating environments. Although deep reinforcement learning (DRL) demonstrates potential in handling randomness, pure data-driven DRL strategies still encounter bottlenecks in terms of action feasibility and model scalability in practical applications. Specifically, during action exploration, the DRL strategy may generate charge and discharge instructions that violate the physical limits of the battery or the user's charge requirements. If such actions are corrected only by simple cropping operations, the overall coordination and accuracy of the scheduling scheme can be easily destroyed. Furthermore, as the number of EVs increases, the state-action space of the centralized DRL architecture grows exponentially, making training difficult or even non-convergent. To address the above issues, this paper proposes a novel integrated DRL framework. This framework features a physics-constrained and scalable architecture that couples market bidding with real-time scheduling. It ensures the feasibility of decisions through an embedded action feasibility repair layer, and achieves computational scalability via a parameter-sharing multi-agent design. The simulation results show that the proposed strategy can alleviate the risks of bid and dispatching deviations caused by market and user uncertainties, and significantly improve the operational benefits of EVAs.

title: Communication Topology Inference and Critical Node Identification of UAV Swarms for Counter-UAV Operations
affiliations: Northwestern Polytechnical University, Northwestern Polytechnical University and Northwestern Polytechnical University

detail.title: Communication Topology Inference and Critical Node Identification of UAV Swarms for Counter-UAV Operations
detail.abstract: UAV swarms have become a prominent threat in modern warfare, yet counter ing them remains challenging. The large scale and rapid deployment of UAV swarms render individual neutralization both costly and impractical. Since UAV swarms depend on communication networks for coordination, disrupting critical nodes within these networks offers a more efficient countermeasure. This, however, requires prior knowledge of the swarm’s communication topol ogy. Existing approaches either rely on communication signals that are difficult to intercept, or overlook the dynamic power adjustment of UAVs, limiting their practical applicability. This paper proposes a non-cooperative topology inference method using only node location and signal power data. The swarm is modeled as a complex network, and the inference problem is cast as a bi-objective optimization balancing network robustness against energy consumption, solved via NSGA-II. Simulations in 3D environments show that the method achieves over 70% inference accuracy across swarms of different scales, providing a viable solution for real-world counter-swarm operations.

title: The Future of Software Development: Navigating the Agentic Revolution and the Training Gap Paradox

detail.title: The Future of Software Development: Navigating the Agentic Revolution and the Training Gap Paradox
detail.abstract: According to global estimates 41% of all code is now AI-generated, with over 97% of developers adopting AI use even ahead of company policies or mandates [1] and even top engineers at Anthropic and OpenAI, such as Boris Cherny, the head of Claude Code, saying AI now writes 100% of their personal code [2]. As agentic AI automates entry-level programming tasks, a “Junior Gap” paradox is emerging: the traditional on-ramps that once built deep engineering judgment are disappearing, threatening long‑term skill development and the talent pipeline. Human oversight remains essential because LLM-based agents suffer from fundamental limitations—including hallucinations [3] [4] and contextual misunderstandings [5]—that make fully autonomous software development unreliable. The combination of reduced entry‑level roles and indispensable human oversight creates a systemic problem: no proven training model yet replaces the experiential learning lost to automation. This paper documents that gap, reviews why existing educational models fall short, and issues a call to action for researchers, industry, and educators to develop and validate new approaches before the profession faces a fragile workforce skilled at prompting but incapable of deep engineering judgment. The industry must also contend with the profound economic, governance, and cultural shifts that accompany AI’s redefinition of software development workflows and workforce dynamics [1] [6].

title: Nighttime Lights as a Proxy for Local Economic Activity: Evidence from Texas Cities
affiliations: University of North Texas - College of Science

detail.title: Nighttime Lights as a Proxy for Local Economic Activity: Evidence from Texas Cities

keywords.keywords: Nighttime lights \sep VIIRS \sep local economic activity \sep municipal nowcasting \sep sales tax \sep Google Earth Engine \sep deep learning

detail.abstract: Nighttime satellite lights are widely used as proxies for economic activity, yet their reliability at fine spatial scales remains less understood. This paper examines whether satellite-derived nighttime lights can proxy high-frequency local economic activity and whether predictive performance varies systematically with city size. Using Google Earth Engine, I construct a monthly panel of Texas cities from 2016 to 2025 that combines VIIRS Day/Night Band radiance measures, $64 \times 64$ nighttime-light image tiles, municipal population, and city-level sales tax allocation data. I compare linear regression, multilayer perceptron, convolutional neural network, and hybrid image-tabular models using a time-based train-validation-test split. The results show that nighttime lights are strongly associated with local sales tax activity, but this relationship is highly scale-dependent. Aggregate models achieve strong overall performance, yet accuracy differs substantially across population groups, indicating that nighttime-light signals are not equally reliable across small and large municipalities. Hybrid models combining aggregate radiance features with spatial image information perform best, suggesting that image-based spatial patterns provide information beyond simple radiance summaries. These findings shift attention from whether lights proxy economic activity to when, where, and at what spatial scale they do so reliably. The paper highlights the importance of city size in high-frequency municipal nowcasting and cautions against assuming uniform predictive validity across local geographies.

title: VITAL: A Validity-aware model for interactive temporal attention learning in destructivecontinuous-time dynamic graphs
affiliations: Konkuk University and Konkuk University

detail.title: VITAL: A Validity-aware model for interactive temporal attention learning in destructivecontinuous-time dynamic graphs
detail.abstract: Continuous-time dynamic graph (CTDG) models commonly predict future interactions by retrieving historical events that are semantically similar to the current query. However, indestructive CTDGs, state-changing or boundary events may invalidate previously observedpositive relations at query time, even when those relations remain semantically similar tothe current query. This phenomenon leads to retrieval contamination, where the attentionmechanism retrieves stale yet plausible historical information and incorporates it into the current representation.To address this issue, we propose VITAL, a validity-aware temporal attention model thatdisentangles semantic retrieval from query-time validity control. VITAL preserves query–patchattention for semantic relevance ranking while introducing a separate validity stream that gates each retrieved patch during value aggregation. This value-level routing mechanism suppresses stale evidence without requiring the attention logits to encode validity information, thereby enabling the model to learn semantic relevance and contextual usefulness jointly.We evaluated VITAL across structural, access-regime, behavioral-regime, and generalCTDG settings. Experimental results on the StarCraft and ACT-MOOC datasets show thatVITAL improves average precision (AP) over DyGFormer by 75.3% and 123.7%, respectively,under random negative sampling, and by 77.3% and 70.2%, respectively, under historical-negative stress settings.

title: Koopman spectral kernel network for non-stationary time series forecasting
affiliations: Southeast University, Southeast University, Southeast University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Koopman spectral kernel network for non-stationary time series forecasting
detail.abstract: The accurate forecasting of non-stationary time series, which are widely observed in various real-world scenarios, holds significant practical importance. Nevertheless, the complex nonlinear dynamics and time-varying characteristics of such time series pose fundamental challenges to developing reliable forecasting models.In this context, Koopman-based approaches have recently achieved promising performance owing to their ability to linearize nonlinear dynamics by mapping original states into high-dimensional space using measurement functions. Despite this progress, existing approaches typically capture only fixed and discrete frequency components through predefined measurement functions, which restrict the ability of models to adapt to time-varying characteristics. To address this issue, we propose Koopman spectral kernel network (KoskerNet), which incorporates deep spectral kernels into the learning of Koopman operators. The integration of deep spectral kernels enables the model to adaptively learn measurement functions and to further capture continuous frequencies of non-stationary time series by the corresponding spectral density. Moreover, a distribution constraint module is introduced to align the distribution of predictions with that of the data, accommodating time-varying statistical characteristics. Consequently, these designs jointly allow KoskerNet to effectively model time-varying characteristics inherent in non-stationary time series. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method.

title: The short-term response of residential customers to long-duration power interruptions
affiliations: University of California, Berkeley - Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab), University of California, Berkeley - Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab), Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and University of California, Berkeley - Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Berkeley Lab)

detail.title: The short-term response of residential customers to long-duration power interruptions
detail.abstract: Increases in the frequency, intensity, and duration of extreme weather events will translate into the potential for widespread, long duration power interruptions with substantial social and economic impacts. This paper fills a gap by using specifically designed surveys to understand the strategic response of residential customers to 1-, 3-, and 14-day interruptions. We find that relocation is 5-10 times more expensive than staying home, but that up to 85% of customers relocate with a 14-day interruption. The economic consequences of these decisions are highly unequal – with lower income customers spending substantial portions of their monthly income to mitigate interruption impacts – and are equivalent to $5 to $25 billion in our case study in the state of Illinois in the United States. We discuss the drivers for the relocation decision, including the fact that customers that own backup generation are significantly less likely to relocate and estimate the impacts on transportation infrastructure due to this relocation. These results can be used by utilities, regulators, planners, and other decision makers to understand the multifaceted nature of mitigation options for resilience enhancements within and outside the power system.

title: MPC-ADMM-Based Rapid Distributed Optimal Allocation Method for Frequency Regulation Power in Large-Scale Wind Farms
affiliations: Shandong University, Shandong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, China Electric Power Research Institute and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: MPC-ADMM-Based Rapid Distributed Optimal Allocation Method for Frequency Regulation Power in Large-Scale Wind Farms
detail.abstract: Responding to system frequency regulation (FR) power commands is a typical multi-wind turbine generator (WTG) coordinated process for a Wind farm (WF), requiring rapid allocation of the power command among WTGs within the WF. However, in large-scale WFs, traditional centralized optimal control suffers from communication delays, a heavy computational burden, and insufficient information synchronization, which hinder rapid online power allocation. To address these issues, a model-prediction control (MPC)-based rapid distributed optimal allocation method for FR power in large-scale WFs is proposed. Firstly, by constructing a rotor speed prediction model for WTGs, an MPC-based optimization model for WF power allocation is formulated to achieve optimal distribution among WTGs, with optimization objectives that include FR power tracking, power smoothness, and rotor speed states. Subsequently, to satisfy the real-time demand for FR power allocation, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) distributed optimization solution incorporating dual-time-scale consistency is proposed to solve the MPC problem, avoiding the computational burden and communication delays caused by the large number of WTGs in traditional centralized control. Finally, a case study demonstrates that the proposed method can effectively track FR power command, compared with conventional centralized control, significantly reducing computational burden while meeting real-time performance requirements. Moreover, it enables an optimal allocation of FR power and smooth recovery of WTG rotor speed.

title: Flood Risk, Information and House Prices: Evidence from Repeat Sales
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Flood Risk, Information and House Prices: Evidence from Repeat Sales
detail.abstract: This paper examines how flood risk is priced in residential property markets using a repeat-sales framework that identifies within-property price adjustments following realised flood events. We combine transaction-level data with realised flood events, a high-resolution expected-loss-based measure of underlying flood risk (FloodScore™), and publicly observable flood-zone classifications, allowing us to distinguish between underlying physical risk and the information channels through which risk becomes relevant for pricing. We find that flood events reduce house-price growth by around 2–3%, with larger effects following recent and repeated events. However, variation in price responses is not explained by detailed measures of underlying flood risk. Once flood-zone classifications are accounted for, model-based flood risk adds little additional explanatory power. Price responses are concentrated in areas where flood risk is publicly identified and institutionally embedded. The findings suggest that flood risk is not continuously priced based on underlying hazard but is instead incorporated through discrete updating following salient flood events and mediated by publicly observable risk signals.​

title: Inflation Beyond Economics: Chronic Economic Instability as a Systemic Cognitive Destabilizer

detail.title: Inflation Beyond Economics: Chronic Economic Instability as a Systemic Cognitive Destabilizer
detail.abstract: This paper proposes that chronic inflationary environments may operate not merely as economic phenomena but as systemic cognitive destabilizers at the societal scale. Drawing on neuropsychology, behavioral economics, and civilizational theory, we argue that prolonged exposure to economic instability is likely to amplify measurable effects on attentional capacity, creative output, long-term planning, and social trust — effects that interact with, and may compound, other structural factors including digital fragmentation, political instability, and institutional erosion. We introduce three conceptual instruments — Cognitive Inflation Stress (CIS), Monetary Neural Fatigue (MNF), and the Survival Brain / Creative Brain axis (SB/CB) — as analytical tools for capturing the neuropsychological costs that chronic inflation may contribute to at the population level. We further propose that societies under sustained economic pressure may undergo a systemic transition from Creative Mode to Survival Mode cognitive processing, with civilizationally significant implications. We present testable hypotheses, historical case comparisons, and a dedicated limitations analysis. The framework is offered as a contribution to the emerging field of Civilizational Neuroeconomics.

title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Worn Surface Evolution Using Convolutional LSTM With Adaptive Filtering and Recursive Multi-Step Prediction
affiliations: Yonsei University, Yonsei University and Yonsei University

detail.title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Worn Surface Evolution Using Convolutional LSTM With Adaptive Filtering and Recursive Multi-Step Prediction
detail.abstract: Reliable prediction of the spatiotemporal evolution ofwear-induced surface topography is critical for assessing the reliability of sliding-contact mechanical components, yet most data-driven studies remain focused on scalar wear indicators. This study presents a Convolutional LSTM(Long Short-Term Memory)-based model that directly forecasts future height maps from limited earlystage time-series observations. The AI contribution is a distribution-aware, KDE (kernel density estimation)-based adaptive filtering rule embedded in recursive multi-step forecasting: the threshold is updated from the incremental-wear density (valley between near-zero noise and wear components) to suppress unworn-region false positives and prevent error accumulation. The engineering application is long-horizon, field-level prediction of worn-surface evolution to complement contact–wear simulations and reduce reliance on full-duration wear testing in reliability assessment and surfacedesign screening. Across recursive prediction up to 10,000 cycles, the proposed framework preserves wear-scar topology and surface statistical trends, achieving SSIM of 0.9904 at 10,000 cycles and tracking cumulative wear volume with an average relative error of 3.94% over 3,500 – 10,000 cycles.

title: Multi-Scale Feature-Enhanced Auto-UNet with Cross Graph Mamba for High Resolution Image Anomaly Detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Multi-Scale Feature-Enhanced Auto-UNet with Cross Graph Mamba for High Resolution Image Anomaly Detection
detail.abstract: High resolution image provides the granular detail necessary for precise Anomaly Detection, but it imposes prohibitive computational burdens on traditional pixel-level processing. While recent advances in Autoencoders, GNNs, and Mamba have shown promise, they face critical bottlenecks: 1)  complex training and suboptimal accuracy; 2) GNNs are prone to overfitting in imbalanced samples; 3) Mamba requires an efficient sorting mechanism. To address these challenges, we propose a Multi-scale Image and Graph Feature Enhanced  Auto-UNet with a novel Cross Graph Mamba. Specifically, our backbone leverages the 2D Discrete Wavelet Transform and its inverse as an autoencoder to decompose images into multi-scale sub-layers. We synergize a Butterworth high-pass operator with graph correlation for dual-domain feature extraction and introduce Top-K Principal Component Analysis prompt tuning and Normalized Simulated Annealing  cross message propagation to enhance segmentation accuracy while reducing training complexity by freezing sub-layer parameters. Furthermore, to address the sequential nature of Mamba, we design an Information Entropy  sorting mechanism to ranks graph correlation  tokens. Finally, we formulate a loss function based on the Gradient Boosting Cosine Similarity of Mahalanobis distances between reconstructed and original images. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets demonstrate our method significantly outperforms SOTAs in both detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: Multi-stage Compound Drought–Heatwave Stress Elevates Cotton Yield-Loss Risk across Contrasting Climate Regimes of the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor
affiliations: Northwest A&F University, Northwest Agricultural and Forestry University - Key Lab of Agricultural Soil and Water Engineering in Arid and Semiarid Areas, Northwest A&F University, Northwest A&F University, National University of Singapore and University of Oulu

detail.title: Multi-stage Compound Drought–Heatwave Stress Elevates Cotton Yield-Loss Risk across Contrasting Climate Regimes of the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor
detail.abstract: Compound drought–heatwave events (CDHEs) are intensifying under non-stationary climate conditions and pose growing risks to agriculture in climate transition zones, yet their evolving characteristics and probabilistic impacts on crop yield remain difficult to capture using stationary frameworks that ignore climatic non-stationarity and carryover effects across crop growth stages. Taking the China–Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) as a case study, we developed a non-stationary framework to quantify CDHE risk evolution from 1981 to 2023 and the associated yield loss of cotton. GAMLSS was combined with a bivariate copula to construct a Non-stationary Standardized Compound Event Index (NSCEI). A correlation-informed AHP was then used to identify the most vulnerable growth stage, and the copula model was applied to estimate conditional yield-loss probabilities under different compound-stress levels. Results show clear regional contrasts: warming increases CDHE risk in Xinjiang, whereas a wetting trend in Pakistan partly offsets the warming effect and keeps compound risk more stable. The flowering–boll-setting stage is the key vulnerability window and is mainly driven by drought severity. Compound stress sustained across multiple growth stages substantially raises the probability of yield loss. In Northern and Southern Xinjiang, the loss probability rises from 27~28% in stress-free seasons to around 67~69% when two or more stages are stressed. In Pakistan, the cumulative response is weaker, with the loss probability increasing from 44% to 57%, but coexisting with a much wider range of individual yield losses. These findings highlight the need for whole-season management rather than single-stage interventions in climatically complex regions.

title: Dual-Path Dual-Discriminator GAN for Tunnel Leakage Detection Using Image Fusion
affiliations: Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing Jiaotong University and Khwaja Fareed University of Engineering & Information Technology

detail.title: Dual-Path Dual-Discriminator GAN for Tunnel Leakage Detection Using Image Fusion
detail.abstract: To overcome the limitations of using a single sensor for detecting tunnel leakage, a tunnel leakage detection method based on Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) that fuses infrared and visible images is proposed. By combining GAN model with Non-Subsampled Shearlet Transform (NSST) and dual-path dual-discriminator architecture, higher-quality leakage images are obtained. An experimental dataset containing 1000 infrared and visible tunnel leakage images is established for training, with experimental validation conducted using 200 sets of tunnel leakage data from Shuangshan Tunnel in Jiulongpo District, Chongqing. The results show that, compared to JLRSD and GAN, the fusion images generated by D-FusionGAN exhibit the highest subjective visibility. Detection based on yolov13, the detection accuracy of the fusion images by D-FusionGAN reaches 79.66%, which is 5.08% higher than infrared detection and 8.24% higher than visible detection. The fusion images effectively mitigate the impact of lighting conditions, exhibit high detection accuracy.

title: A new method for preliminary design of deep tunnel in highly fractured rock masses: Part 1: Development of surrogate models
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Lorraine, University of Lorraine and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A new method for preliminary design of deep tunnel in highly fractured rock masses: Part 1: Development of surrogate models
detail.abstract: During the early stages of a deep tunnel design, it is essential to correctly identify the potential geological and geotechnical hazards and to demonstrate the possibility to overcome them despite significant uncertainties. One of these critical hazards in poor rock masses is the occurrence of large radial deformations, often referred to as squeezing. If such a risk is identified, a relevant design strategy must then be developed. The technical solutions considered and thus the design are highly dependent on the amount of expected large deformation and its interaction with the support system. However, during preliminary design, it can be difficult to correctly assess this interaction, as significant uncertainties exist regarding geology and geotechnical parameters. Moreover, the existing methods are either not well adapted or too complex to use at this stage. To overcome these limitations, a new method is proposed based on surrogate models derived from a large number of 2D axisymmetric numerical calculations covering a wide range of geological conditions potentially associated with large radial deformations. This paper (Part 1) aims to present the methodology used to create these surrogate models, the resulting models, and their graphical representations designed to facilitate practical use. The models allow estimation of the ground pressure on the support far from the face, as well as the radial strain occurring between the face and the installation of the rigid support. The proposed surrogate models are easy to use, precise enough for preliminary design, and well situated for the explicit introduction and propagation of uncertainties which is addressed in Part 2 of this study.

title: A seismic reflection data-driven active learning approach for optimizing in-situ penetration testing layouts
affiliations: Dalian University of Technology, Dalian University of Technology and Dalian University of Technology

detail.title: A seismic reflection data-driven active learning approach for optimizing in-situ penetration testing layouts
detail.abstract: High-precision site characterization with low uncertainty is essential for the reliable design of offshore wind foundations. However, it is frequently constrained by sparse in-situ testing locations and high investigation costs. To address this challenge, an active learning-driven sequential sampling approach is proposed to optimize the spatial layout of in-situ penetration tests. The proposed method integrates a previously developed physics-informed deep learning model, utilizing seismic reflection data to efficiently extrapolate 1D penetration data into 2D or 3D spatial profiles. The sampling optimization is systematically executed in three phases. First, initial testing locations are strategically prioritized in regions exhibiting high stratigraphic complexity, using the mean value of the absolute seismic reflection amplitude as a quantitative indicator. Second, for the selection of supplementary locations, two active learning strategies are proposed, comprising an "inter-layer reflection amplitude" strategy that rapidly identifies hidden strata during early iterations and a "predictive uncertainty" strategy that effectively minimizes global site errors during later stages. Third, to prevent redundant exploration, a joint termination criterion combining the moving average convergence (MAC) criterion and the consecutive no-improvement (CNI) criterion is introduced to objectively halt the sampling process when the marginal information gain diminishes. Validations through a numerical example and the N-10 offshore wind farm project demonstrate that the proposed method effectively eliminates highly redundant testing locations, yielding approximately a 40% reduction in in-situ testing costs without compromising site characterization precision. Foundation bearing capacity evaluations based on the predicted cone tip resistance (qc) reveal that the error for lateral bearing capacity is strictly controlled within 10%, while the true vertical bearing capacity is enveloped within a 95% confidence interval, confirming the practical utility of the approach for preliminary engineering design.

title: Demand Dependence-aware Stochastic Joint Replenishment Policies via Deep Reinforcement Learning
affiliations: McMaster University, McMaster University and University of Calgary

detail.title: Demand Dependence-aware Stochastic Joint Replenishment Policies via Deep Reinforcement Learning
detail.abstract: We study a stochastic joint replenishment problem (SJRP) in which product demands are dependent across items and over time. Unlike traditional models that assume independent demands, we consider a setting where current demands depend on historical observations across items and contextual information. To address this problem, we propose a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) architecture with a gated and factorized action design tailored to multi-item systems with shared setup costs. We then conduct an empirical study to assess when this structured design is beneficial relative to non-gated PPO, Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) and optimized classical policies. Experiments on synthetic data, real immunoglobulin demand and M5 sales show that the proposed approach significantly reduces costs, particularly in scenarios with moderate to high joint ordering costs. It achieves over 80% improvement over classical baselines on synthetic and immunoglobulin datasets and up to 30% improvement on M5 instances. The findings highlight the effectiveness of gated DRL architectures for addressing decision coupling in joint replenishment systems with interdependent and uncertain demand.

title: A Performance Comparison of Physics-Based and Nature-Inspired Algorithms for Double-Layer Barrel Vault Optimization
affiliations: Islamic Azad University

detail.title: A Performance Comparison of Physics-Based and Nature-Inspired Algorithms for Double-Layer Barrel Vault Optimization
detail.abstract: The growing application of metaheuristic algorithms as intelligent search tools underscores the importance of selecting appropriate methods, as each algorithm exhibits distinct strengths and limitations. Accordingly, comparing algorithms within a fair and uniform framework facilitates the identification of the most suitable approach. In this study, two major classes of metaheuristic optimization algorithms are systematically investigated for structural optimization purposes: physics-based approaches, including the Newton–Raphson–Based Optimizer (NRBO), Ray Optimization (RO), and Improved Ray Optimization (IRO); and nature-inspired approaches, consisting of the Starfish Optimization Algorithm (SFOA), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Democratic Particle Swarm Optimization (DPSO). The algorithms are applied to the weight minimization of two large-scale double-layer barrel vault structures under stress and displacement constraints. Numerical results demonstrate that although DPSO converges more slowly, it outperforms conventional PSO in terms of maximum nodal displacement and stress ratio. Moreover, IRO significantly improves the efficiency and solution quality of the original RO, while NRBO generally produces conservative designs. Overall, SFOA and DPSO consistently deliver the most competitive and reliable solutions among the examined algorithms.

title: Instance-Conditioned Modality Fusion for Multi-Modal Entity Alignment
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics

detail.title: Instance-Conditioned Modality Fusion for Multi-Modal Entity Alignment
detail.abstract: Multi-modal entity alignment (MMEA) identifies equivalent entities across different knowledge graphs by fusing multiple sources of information, including graph structure, relations, attributes, and images. Existing methods either use global fusion weights that ignore entity-level differences or learn implicit coefficients through attention mechanisms, lacking explicit modeling and stabilization of entity-level modality contribution. We propose Instance-Conditioned Modality Fusion (ICMF), which uses a lightweight ReliabilityNet to generate a fusion contribution score $q$ independently for each entity--modality pair. After normalization, the scores are directly used as fusion weights, enabling entity-level adaptive multi-modal fusion. To suppress the tendency of these scores to drift toward extreme distributions under end-to-end positive feedback, we further introduce Dual-Variable Dispersion Control (DVDC), which adaptively constrains the upper bound of score dispersion through Lagrangian dual optimization and stabilizes entity-level contribution learning. Three-seed experiments on three benchmark datasets show that ICMF achieves the best results among the evaluated baselines, with larger gains in low-resource settings. Further analyses show that the learned $q$ is interpretable and that its cross-modal differentiation matches dataset-specific modality characteristics. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/yaolidong/ICMF.

title: Towards Robust Stock Prediction via Logic-enhanced Variational Alpha Synthesis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Peng Cheng Laboratory

detail.title: Towards Robust Stock Prediction via Logic-enhanced Variational Alpha Synthesis
detail.abstract: Formulaic alpha synthesis has emerged as a central problem in quantitative finance, where the goal is to construct predictive signals in the form of formulaic expressions that capture asset return patterns. However, existing approaches typically overlook the non-stationarity of financial markets and fail to embed the market information appropriately, leading to brittle performance under varying market regimes. In this paper, we propose Lovas (Logic-enhanced Variational Alpha Synthesis), a novel neural–symbolic framework for robust stock prediction. Lovas integrates a symbolic regime analyzer with a neural alpha synthesizer: for a specific time step, the symbolic regime analyzer predicts the latent market regime and assigns ensemble weights for the alpha pool, while the alpha synthesizer learns specialized formulaic alphas conditioned on these regimes. Since the market regimes are hidden variables, we therefore formulate alpha synthesis as a variational inference problem and optimize it via a variational EM algorithm.  This design enables Lovas to handle market regime shifts more robustly by explicitly conditioning alpha synthesis on different market categories, therefore achieving much better prediction results. Empirical results on multiple stock benchmarks demonstrate that Lovas consistently outperforms state-of-the-art alpha synthesis methods by achieving better prediction accuracy.

title: HGTFNet: A Hybrid Graph-enhanced Time-Frequency Network for Multivariate Short-Term Electric Load Forecasting
affiliations: Jiangsu University, Jiangsu University, Anhui University, Anhui University, City University of Hong Kong and Griffith University

detail.title: HGTFNet: A Hybrid Graph-enhanced Time-Frequency Network for Multivariate Short-Term Electric Load Forecasting
detail.abstract: Short-term electric load forecasting (STLF) is essential for efficient power system operation, yet existing deep learning models often struggle to simultaneously capture high-frequency transient fluctuations and complex inter-variable dependencies in multivariate load data, leading to over-smoothing and structural distortion. To address these challenges, we propose a Hybrid Graph-enhanced Time-Frequency Network (HGTFNet) that jointly improves numerical accuracy and morphological and spectral fidelity, where fidelity is assessed by waveform morphology (DTW) and harmonic energy distribution (nSpecMAE). HGTFNet adopts a dual-path spectral–temporal architecture that integrates an inverted Transformer backbone with an explicit frequency-domain branch, enabling decoupling of periodic components and stochastic fluctuations while mitigating high-frequency attenuation. A dynamic graph learning module further models cross-variable dependencies to enforce synchronized evolution across multiple load series. In addition, an adaptive temporal query mechanism and a multi-scale convolution module align non-stationary periodic phases and capture fine-grained local variations. Experiments on a real-world urban load dataset (three supply zones) show that HGTFNet consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across multiple horizons, achieving up to a 21.2% reduction in MAPE compared to iTransformer. Beyond point-wise accuracy, HGTFNet improves fidelity, with up to a 13.7% reduction in DTW and lower nSpecMAE, supported by frequency-domain visualizations. Sensitivity analysis further indicates that performance gains arise from adaptive synergy between temporal and frequency representations rather than any single module. Overall, by effectively alleviating over-smoothing and preserving transient peak dynamics, HGTFNet provides a structurally consistent and robust forecasting solution, offering reliable support for secure grid operation and efficient energy management under complex load conditions.

title: Shannon--Neumann Least Action Principle: Normatively Constrained Epistemic-Utility Dynamics in Cognitive AI
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Shannon--Neumann Least Action Principle: Normatively Constrained Epistemic-Utility Dynamics in Cognitive AI
detail.abstract: We propose a variational framework for cognitive AI in which adaptive behavior emerges from minimizing a normatively constrained epistemic–utility action over trajectories. The resulting Shannon–Neumann Least Action Principle (SN-LAP) unifies three core components of intelligent systems: information acquisition (epistemic learning), goal-directed optimization (utility), and constraint satisfaction (normative alignment). We derive both discrete- and continuous-time formulations, showing that SN-LAP induces tractable update rules closely related to entropy-regularized and multi-objective reinforcement learning. The continuous limit yields Euler--Lagrange equations governing cognitive dynamics, while regularization introduces second-order dynamics with momentum and dissipation. We establish existence of extremal trajectories and analyze stability via Lyapunov methods, demonstrating that dissipation induces convergence to norm-compliant equilibria. We further show that symmetries of the SN-action give rise to conserved quantities analogous to Noether charges, providing a principled interpretation of persistent exploratory behavior. A minimal tabular MDP experiment illustrates how normative terms systematically trade off performance and constraint satisfaction, recovering standard reinforcement learning as a special case.SN-LAP provides a unified, trajectory-level perspective linking variational inference, energy-based models, and reinforcement learning, offering a principled foundation for designing adaptive and normatively aligned AI systems.

title: Upgrade or Evade: Heterogeneous Firm Responses to Foreign Environmental Regulations
affiliations: Xi’an Jiaotong University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Upgrade or Evade: Heterogeneous Firm Responses to Foreign Environmental Regulations
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how destination-market environmental regulation reshapes exporters’ environmental performance and strategic trade patterns. Exploiting the implementation of the EU’s WEEE and RoHS directives as a quasi-natural experiment, we employ a difference-in-differences design with continuous treatment intensity using comprehensive Chinese firm-level data. We find that while the directives reduce aggregate emission intensity, this average effect masks profound firm-level heterogeneity. High-productivity firms achieve emission reductions primarily by augmenting investment in end-of-pipe abatement and enhancing treatment efficiency. In contrast, low-productivity firms exhibit negligible abatement adjustments and instead reallocate exports toward less regulated destinations. We rationalize these patterns within a Melitz-style framework where destination-specific compliance costs induce a sorting mechanism: high-productivity firms internalize abatement costs to retain market access, while low-productivity firms exit the regulated market. Consequently, while destination-based regulation succeeds in cleaning up supply chains for developed markets, it inadvertently deepens the North-South environmental divide. The strategic diversion of dirty exports by laggard firms highlights a critical trade-off: unilateral standards drive upgrading at the top but trigger pollution leakage at the bottom, shifting the environmental burden to developing nations.

title: Dirty Chasing or Data Cheating? The Environmental Trade-offs of Meeting GDP Targets in China
affiliations: Hunan University, Hunan University and City University of Macau

detail.title: Dirty Chasing or Data Cheating? The Environmental Trade-offs of Meeting GDP Targets in China
detail.abstract: Does the high-powered incentive of GDP targeting come at an unintended environmental cost? Using Chinese prefecture-level panel data from 2003 to 2023, we construct a bunching-ITT framework to quantify the environmental externalities of target-based GDP manipulation. We document that manipulation to the GDP target completion threshold significantly elevates both the levels and intensities of regional SO2and CO2emissions. Mechanism tests establish that these environmental costs arise primarily from two forms of substantive dirty chasing: the strategic environmental deregulation and short-termism in resource allocation, rather than mere statistical cheating. Heterogeneity analysis explores the differential effects of institutional constraints and official characteristics on manipulation incentives and their environmental consequences. On the incentive side, cadre evaluation reforms and flexible target-setting significantly reduce the probability of manipulation. On the consequences side, the environmental externalities of GDP manipulation are less pronounced in cities led by officials in their promotion window or approaching retirement, as well as in regions subject to central environmental inspections. Our findings provide micro-level causal evidence on the agency costs and behavioral distortions embedded in China's target-based governance system.

title: Can Automation Reshape Demographics? The Effect of Robots on Fertility Rates and Sex Ratio Imbalance in China
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Peking University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Can Automation Reshape Demographics? The Effect of Robots on Fertility Rates and Sex Ratio Imbalance in China
detail.abstract: This study examines how automation shapes fertility transitions in China, focusing on within-marriage births and sex ratio at birth. Using a Bartik IV combined with first difference in nationally representative household panel data, we find that greater robot exposure reduces within-marriage fertility and lowers the likelihood of additional births when prior children are all girls. Effects are larger in regions with more traditional cultural norms and among younger, less-educated women. Mechanism evidence is consistent with a dominant substitution effect as women’s relative wages rise. Quantity–quality considerations appear less important for overall fertility but may affect the gender-composition margin.

title: The migration law of platinum group metals and ultrasonic assisted leaching in the process of selective dissolution and iron enrichment of Fe-PGMs alloy

detail.title: The migration law of platinum group metals and ultrasonic assisted leaching in the process of selective dissolution and iron enrichment of Fe-PGMs alloy
detail.abstract: The concentration of Fe-PGMs, an intermediate product obtained through pyrometallurgical capture from waste automotive catalysts, is an important pathway for the efficient recycling and utilization of platinum group metals as secondary resources, which brings both economic and environmental benefits. In this study, the occurrence states of Pt, Pd, and Rh in Fe-PGMs alloy were characterized. The migration law of PGMs and the dissolution kinetics of Fe were analyzed by acid leaching experiments. Based on the results, an ultrasonic-assisted selective iron removal and platinum group metal enrichment process was proposed. The results reveal that with the increase of PGMs content, Pd precipitates as high-purity second-phase particles. Compared with hydrochloric acid, sulfuric acid can significantly inhibit the dissolution of Pt and Pd. The introduction of ultrasound in sulfuric acid enhances the interfacial mass transfer efficiency, and ascorbic acid acts as a potential buffer to inhibit the dissolution of Rh induced by micro-galvanic corrosion. Under the optimum conditions, the concentration of Fe in the leaching solution increased from 39.05 g/L to 58.33 g/L, and the concentration of Rh decreased from 23.7 mg/L to 2.6 mg/L. After enrichment, the platinum group metal grade of Fe-PGMs alloy increased from 0.51% to 6.04% and 6.85% to 23.6%. Finally, 99% of Rh in the leaching solution was recovered by zinc powder displacement method. This study provides an efficient and industrial application prospect of PGMs concentration technology route.

title: Out of sight, out of mind: Informal used vehicle trade as a blind spot in EV transition governance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of California, Davis

detail.title: Out of sight, out of mind: Informal used vehicle trade as a blind spot in EV transition governance
detail.abstract: International trade in second-hand vehicles (SHVs) plays an important but poorly documented role in shaping vehicle fleets and material flows. In North America, large numbers of vehicles are informally exported from the US to Mexico and remain absent from official trade statistics. This study quantifies these hidden flows using a novel modeling framework integrating field survey data, literature benchmarks, and administrative records within a US–Mexico vehicle stock turnover model. Results indicate that formal and informal SHV exports represent 12–15% of annual US vehicle retirements, while informal imports add an estimated 24–45% to vehicles entering the Mexican fleet. By 2050, nearly 30% of cumulative US end-of-life EV battery mass may exit the country embedded in SHV exports. These findings identify informal SHV trade as a blind spot in EV transition governance and point to upstream markets, particularly salvage vehicle auctions, as a strategic regulatory opportunity to improve transparency and battery circularity.

title: Irrigation Transformation in India: Assessing the Impact of PMKSY Using Counterfactual Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Institute for Social and Economic Change (ISEC)

detail.title: Irrigation Transformation in India: Assessing the Impact of PMKSY Using Counterfactual Analysis
detail.abstract: Irrigation plays a critical role in enhancing agricultural productivity, stabilising farm incomes, supporting multiple cropping systems, and ensuring food security in India. Despite substantial public investments in irrigation infrastructure over the decades, irrigation development in India has continued to face several challenges, including uneven regional distribution, inefficient water use, inadequate convergence among irrigation schemes, and limited expansion of assured irrigation in rain-fed areas. In order to address these constraints and promote efficient water management, the Government of India launched the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) during 2015–16 with the objective of expanding irrigation coverage, improving water-use efficiency, and ensuring ”Har Khet Ko Pani” (water to every farm). Against this background, the present study evaluates the impact of PMKSY on irrigation development in India using a comprehensive time-series analytical framework.The study is based on secondary data collected from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Agricultural Statistics at a Glance, and other official government sources for the period from 2005–06 to 2022–23. To examine the effectiveness of PMKSY, the study analyses major irrigation indicators, including net irrigated area, gross irrigated area, proportion of gross irrigated area to gross cropped area, and irrigation intensity. The analysis divides the study period into pre-PMKSY (2005–2014) and post-PMKSY (2015–2023) phases in order to compare irrigation performance before and after the implementation of the programme.The study employs a combination of descriptive statistics, mean comparison tests, trend regression models, interrupted time series analysis, structural break tests, and counterfactual impact estimation techniques to assess the extent of change associated with PMKSY. The results reveal substantial improvement in all major irrigation indicators during the post-PMKSY period. The mean net irrigated area increased from 59.61 million hectares in the pre-PMKSY period to 71.20 million hectares in the post-PMKSY period, while gross irrigated area increased from 83.36 million hectares to 106.60 million hectares. Similarly, irrigation intensity and the share of irrigated area in gross cropped area also recorded significant improvement after the introduction of the scheme.The interrupted time series analysis indicates that the annual growth rate of net irrigated area accelerated significantly after the implementation of PMKSY, suggesting a clear structural shift in irrigation trends. The structural break analysis further confirms the existence of a statistically significant break around 2015, coinciding with the launch of PMKSY. Counterfactual estimates demonstrate that actual irrigation expansion substantially exceeded the projected no-intervention scenario, and the gap between actual and counterfactual irrigation coverage widened progressively over time, indicating cumulative policy effects.Overall, the findings suggest that PMKSY has played a significant role in strengthening irrigation infrastructure, expanding irrigation coverage, and promoting irrigation-led agricultural development in India. The study highlights the importance of sustained public investment in irrigation, improved water management practices, and the expansion of micro-irrigation systems, particularly in water-scarce and rain-fed regions. title: WLNO: Wavelet-Laplace Neural Operator for Solving Partial Differential Equations
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Oklahoma State University

detail.title: WLNO: Wavelet-Laplace Neural Operator for Solving Partial Differential Equations
detail.abstract: This work introduces the Wavelet-Laplace Neural Operator (WLNO), a novel neural operator thatfuses Haar wavelet multi-scale spatial decomposition with the Laplace-domain pole-residueformulation of the Laplace Neural Operator (LNO). While LNO captures transient and steady-statedynamics through learnable system poles and residues, it lacks an explicit mechanism for extractingspatially localized multi-scale features inherent in complex PDE solutions. WLNO addresses thisby augmenting the LNO core with a parallel single-level Haar discrete wavelet transform (DWT)branch that decomposes the lifted feature map into four frequency subbands: approximation (LL),horizontal detail (LH), vertical detail (HL), and diagonal detail (HH) and applies independentlearned $1\times1$ convolutions to each subband before reconstruction via the inverse DWT. Thetwo branches are fused through a learnable sigmoid-gated weight $\alpha_\mathrm{wav}$,initialized to give a small initial contribution to the wavelet branch, allowing the model toadaptively balance Laplace-domain dynamics against spatial multi-scale features throughouttraining. WLNO is evaluated against LNO on five benchmark PDE problems using identicalhyperparameters, training data, and evaluation protocols: the diffusion equation, the Burgersequation, the reaction-diffusion system, Darcy flow, and the two-dimensional Navier-Stokesequation. WLNO consistently outperforms LNO on all five problems with the most pronounced improvement on problems with strong spatial multi-scalestructure, such as the Burgers equation with sharp shock fronts and the Navier-Stokes equationwith coherent vortical structures, while remaining consistent across smoother and ellipticproblems. These results demonstrate that wavelet-based multi-scale spatial decomposition is aprincipled and effective complement to Laplace-domain operator learning.

title: An Enterprise Architecture-Based AI TRiSM Framework for DataPrivacy Compliance Monitoring in National Cybersecurity Agencies
